translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, Xiao Zhengbiao, Xiao Zhi, Xiao Tui, Xiao Tai, Xiao Hui, Xiao Yuansu, Xiao Dahuan
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, Xiao Zhengbiao, Xiao Zhi, Xiao Tui, Xiao Tai, Xiao Hui, Xiao Yuansu, and Xiao Dahuan

sentences.zh: 列傳第十七

translations.literal: Biographies 17
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 17

sentences.zh: 司馬休之司馬楚之曾孫裔司馬景之司馬叔璠司馬天助劉昶蕭寶夤兄子贊蕭正表蕭祗蕭退蕭泰蕭捴蕭圓肅蕭大圜

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, great-grandson Yi, Sima Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, Sima Tianzhu, Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, nephew Zan, Xiao Zhengbiao, Xiao Zhi, Xiao Tui, Xiao Tai, Xiao Hui, Xiao Yuansu, Xiao Dahuan
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, great-grandson Yi, Sima Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, Sima Tianzhu, Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, nephew Zan, Xiao Zhengbiao, Xiao Zhi, Xiao Tui, Xiao Tai, Xiao Hui, Xiao Yuansu, and Xiao Dahuan

sentences.zh: 司馬休之，字季豫，河內溫人，晉宣帝季弟譙王進之後也。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi, styled Jiyu, was a man of Wen in Henei, a descendant of Prince of Qiao Jin, youngest brother of Emperor Xuan of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, styled Jiyu, was from Wen in Henei, descended from Prince Jin of Qiao, youngest brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 晉度江之後，進子孫襲封譙王。

translations.literal: After the Jin crossed the Yangzi, Jin's descendants inherited the fief of Prince of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin crossed south, the line of Prince Jin held the Qiao title in succession.

sentences.zh: 至休之父恬，為鎮北將軍、青兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: By Xiuzhi's time his father Tian was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Yan Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's father Tian was General Who Pacifies the North and dual Inspector of Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 天興五年，休之為荊州刺史，被桓玄逼逐，遂奔慕容德。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxing, Xiuzhi was Inspector of Jing Province; driven out by Huan Xuan, he fled to Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing year 5 he governed Jing until Huan Xuan expelled him and he fled to Murong De.

sentences.zh: 及玄誅，還建業，復為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xuan was executed, he returned to Jiankang and again became Inspector of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan's death he returned to Jiankang and resumed the Jing inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 休之頗得江漢人心。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi had won considerable favor among the people of the Jiang and Han region.
translations.idiomatic: He had won deep goodwill along the Jiang and Han.

sentences.zh: 其子文思繼其兄尚之為譙王，謀圖劉裕。

translations.literal: His son Wensi succeeded his elder brother Shangzhi as Prince of Qiao and plotted against Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wensi succeeded elder brother Shangzhi as Prince of Qiao and plotted against Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕執送休之，令為其所。

translations.literal: Yu seized Xiuzhi and sent him forward, making him act at Yu's bidding.
translations.idiomatic: Yu seized him and used him as his instrument.

sentences.zh: 休之表廢文思，並與裕書陳謝。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized to depose Wensi and also wrote Yu a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi petitioned to depose Wensi and wrote Yu apologizing.

sentences.zh: 神瑞中，裕收休之子文寶、兄子文祖並殺之，乃討休之。

translations.literal: In the Shenrui era Yu seized Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and his nephew Wenzu and killed them, then marched against Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenrui, Yu killed Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and nephew Wenzu, then attacked Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 休之與魯宗之及宗之子軌起兵討裕。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi with Lu Zongzhi and Zongzhi's son Gui raised troops to attack Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi joined Lu Zongzhi and Zongzhi's son Gui in arms against Yu.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，遂與子文思及宗之奔姚興。

translations.literal: Defeated, he fled with his son Wensi and Zongzhi to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Beaten, he fled with Wensi and Zongzhi to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 裕滅姚泓，休之與文思及晉河間王子道賜等數百人皆將妻子降長孫嵩。

translations.literal: When Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Xiuzhi with Wensi and several hundred men including Jin Prince of Hejian Zidaosi all brought wives and children and surrendered to Changsun Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Xiuzhi, Wensi, Prince Zidaosi of Hejian, and hundreds more surrendered to Changsun Song with their families.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征西大將軍、右光祿大夫、始平公，諡曰聲。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Grand General Who Conquers the West, Right Grandee of Splendid Virtue, Duke of Shiping, posthumous name Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Grand General Who Conquers the West, Right Grandee of Splendid Virtue, Duke of Shiping, posthumous name Sheng.

sentences.zh: 文思與淮南公國璠、池陽子道賜不平，而偽親之。

translations.literal: Wensi was at odds with Duke of Huainan Guo Fan and Pool-Yang Zidaosi, yet feigned closeness with them.
translations.idiomatic: Wensi disliked Duke Guo Fan of Huainan and Zidaosi of Chiyang but pretended friendship.

sentences.zh: 國璠性疏直，因醉欲外叛。

translations.literal: Guo Fan was blunt by nature; drunk, he wished to defect outward.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Fan was blunt; drunk once, he meant to flee.

sentences.zh: 文思告之，皆坐誅。

translations.literal: Wensi reported them; all were executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Wensi informed; all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 以文思為廷尉，賜爵郁林公。

translations.literal: Wensi was made Minister of Justice and enfeoffed Duke of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Wensi became Minister of Justice and Duke of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 文思善於其職，聽斷，百姓不得匿其情。

translations.literal: Wensi was skilled in his office; in hearing cases the people could not hide their circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at his post; in court the people could not conceal the facts.

sentences.zh: 進爵譙王，位懷荒鎮將，薨。

translations.literal: Advanced to Prince of Qiao, he held the post of General Who Pacifies the Wilderness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Prince of Qiao and General Who Pacifies the Wilderness, then died.

sentences.zh: 司馬楚之，字德秀，晉宣弟太常馗之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Sima Chuzhi, styled Dexiu, was an eighth-generation descendant of Grand Commandant Kui, younger brother of Emperor Xuan of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chuzhi, styled Dexiu, was eight generations from Grand Commandant Kui, Jin Emperor Xuan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 父榮期，晉益州刺史，為其參軍楊承祖所殺。

translations.literal: His father Rongqi was Jin Inspector of Yi Province and was killed by his aide Yang Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rongqi, Jin's Yi Inspector, was killed by aide Yang Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 楚之時年十七，送父喪還丹楊。

translations.literal: Chuzhi was then seventeen; he escorted his father's coffin back to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi was seventeen and bore his father's coffin back to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 會劉裕誅夷司馬氏，叔父宣期、兄貞之並遇害。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu exterminated the Sima clan, his uncle Xuanqi and elder brother Zhenzhi were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu purged the Simas, uncle Xuanqi and brother Zhenzhi perished.

sentences.zh: 楚之乃逃，匿諸沙門中，濟江至汝、潁間。

translations.literal: Chuzhi fled and hid among monks, crossed the river to the Ru and Ying region.
translations.idiomatic: He hid among monks, crossed the river, and reached the Ru–Ying country.

sentences.zh: 楚之少有英氣，能折節待士。

translations.literal: Chuzhi from youth had heroic spirit and could humble himself to treat scholars.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had heroic bearing and knew how to win men by courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及宋受禪，規欲報復。

translations.literal: When Song received the mandate, he planned revenge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song took the throne he plotted vengeance.

sentences.zh: 收眾據長社，歸之者常萬餘人。

translations.literal: He gathered followers and held Changshe; those who came to him often numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He held Changshe with more than ten thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 宋武深憚之，遣刺客沐謙圖害楚之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song feared him deeply and sent the assassin Mu Qian to plot his death.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Emperor Wu sent the assassin Mu Qian against him.

sentences.zh: 楚之待謙甚厚。

translations.literal: Chuzhi treated Qian with great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi treated Qian with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 謙夜詐疾，知楚之必來，欲因殺之。

translations.literal: Qian feigned illness by night, knowing Chuzhi would surely come, intending to kill him when he did.
translations.idiomatic: Qian feigned sickness at night, sure Chuzhi would visit and meaning to strike then.

sentences.zh: 楚之聞謙病，果自齎湯藥往省之。

translations.literal: Hearing Qian was ill, Chuzhi indeed brought soup and medicine himself to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the illness, Chuzhi came in person with soup and medicine.

sentences.zh: 謙感其意，出匕首于席下，以狀告，遂委身以事之。

translations.literal: Qian was moved by his intent, produced a dagger from beneath the mat, told the whole plan, and thereupon devoted himself to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Qian drew the dagger from under the mat, confessed the plot, and served him thereafter.

sentences.zh: 其推誠信物，得士心，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His pushing sincerity and trusting things—winning men's hearts—were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Winning hearts by sincerity was always his way.

sentences.zh: 明元末，山陽公奚斤略地河南，楚之遣使請降，授荊州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Mingyuan, Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin overran Henan; Chuzhi sent envoys to surrender and was made Inspector of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Mingyuan, Duke Xi Jin of Shanyang took Henan; Chuzhi surrendered and was made Jing Inspector.

sentences.zh: 奚斤既平河南，以楚之所率人戶，分置汝南、汝陽、南頓、新蔡四郡，以益豫州。

translations.literal: When Xi Jin had pacified Henan, Chuzhi's following in households was distributed into the four commanderies Runan, Ruyang, Nandun, and Xincai to enlarge Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Henan fell, his households were split among Runan, Ruyang, Nandun, and Xincai to swell Yu.

sentences.zh: 太武初，楚之遣妻子內居於鄴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiwu, Chuzhi sent wife and children to live within at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiwu he sent family to live inside at Ye.

sentences.zh: 尋征入朝，授安南大將軍，封琅邪王，以拒宋師。

translations.literal: Soon summoned to court, he was made Grand General Who Pacifies the South, enfeoffed Prince of Langye, to resist the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon at court he was Grand General Who Pacifies the South and Prince of Langye against Song.

sentences.zh: 賜前後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: He was granted front and rear guard musicians.
translations.idiomatic: He received front and rear guard musicians.

sentences.zh: 破宋將到彥之別軍於長社。

translations.literal: He defeated a detached force of the Song general Dao Yanzhi at Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Song general Dao Yanzhi's detached force at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 又與冠軍安頡攻拔滑台，禽宋將硃修之、李元德及東郡太守申謨，俘萬餘人。

translations.literal: Again with Champion An Qi he stormed and took Huatai, capturing Song generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande and Administrator of Dongjun Shen Mo, with more than ten thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: With Champion An Qi he took Huatai, capturing Zhu Xiuzhi, Li Yuande, Dongjun's Shen Mo, and over ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 上疏求更進討，太武以兵久勞，不從，以散騎常侍征還。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to advance further in attack; Taiwu, because the army had long been weary, did not agree and recalled him as Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to press the attack; Taiwu, the troops weary, refused and recalled him as Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 宋將裴方明、胡崇之寇仇池。

translations.literal: Song generals Pei Fangming and Hu Chongzhi invaded Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Song generals Pei Fangming and Hu Chongzhi attacked Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 楚之與淮南公皮豹子等督關中諸軍擊走方明，禽崇之。

translations.literal: Chuzhi with Duke of Huainan Pi Baozi and others supervised the Guanzhong armies, routed Fangming, and captured Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi with Duke Pi Baozi of Huainan commanded Guanzhong forces, routed Fangming, and took Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 仇池平而還。

translations.literal: Chouchi was pacified and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chouchi pacified, he returned.

sentences.zh: 車駕征蠕蠕，楚之與濟陰公盧中山等督運以繼大軍。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned against the Rouran, Chuzhi with Duke of Jiyin Lu Zhongshan and others supervised transport to follow the great army.
translations.idiomatic: On the Rouran campaign Chuzhi with Duke Lu Zhongshan of Jiyin directed supply trains for the main host.

sentences.zh: 時鎮北將軍封遝亡入蠕蠕，說令擊楚之以絕糧運。

translations.literal: At the time General Who Pacifies the North Feng Dang had fled into the Rouran and urged them to strike Chuzhi to cut off grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: General Feng Dang had fled to the Rouran and urged them to hit Chuzhi and sever supplies.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕乃遣覘楚之軍，截驢耳而去。

translations.literal: The Rouran then sent scouts to Chuzhi's army, cut off donkeys' ears, and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran scouted his camp, clipped donkeys' ears, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 有告失驢耳者，楚之曰：「必覘賊截之為驗耳，賊將至矣。

translations.literal: When someone reported the lost donkeys' ears, Chuzhi said: "Surely the scouts cut them as proof—the enemy is coming.
translations.idiomatic: Told of the clipped ears, Chuzhi said, "Scouts took them as proof—the foe is near.

sentences.zh: 」乃伐柳為城，灌水令凍，城立而賊至，不可攻逼，乃走散。

translations.literal: " He then felled willows for a wall, poured water to freeze it; the wall stood and the enemy came but could not storm it and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He felled willows, flooded them to ice a wall; when the enemy came they could not breach it and broke away.

sentences.zh: 太武聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: Taiwu heard and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu heard and praised him.

sentences.zh: 尋拜假節、侍中、鎮西大將軍、開府儀同三司、雲中鎮大將、朔州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was given acting credentials, made Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Grand Marshal with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, Grand General of the Yunzhong Garrison, and Inspector of Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon acting credentials, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Grand Marshal equal to the Three Excellencies, Yunzhong commander, and Shuo Inspector.

sentences.zh: 金龍初納太尉、隴西王源賀女。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jinlong he married the daughter of Grand Commandant and Duke of Longxi Yuan He.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinlong's opening he wed Grand Commandant Yuan He's daughter, Duchess of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 生子延宗，次纂，次悅。

translations.literal: He had sons Yanzong, next Zuan, next Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Yanzong, then Zuan, then Yue.

sentences.zh: 後娶沮渠氏，生子徽亮，即河西王沮渠牧犍女，太武妹武威公主所生也。

translations.literal: Later he took a Juqu wife and had son Huiliang—that was the daughter of Hexi King Juqu Mujian, born of Taiwu's sister Princess Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Later a Juqu wife bore Huiliang—daughter of King Juqu Mujian of Hexi, child of Taiwu's sister Princess Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 有寵于文明太后，故以徽亮襲。

translations.literal: Favored by Empress Dowager Wenming, Huiliang therefore inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Favored by Empress Dowager Wenming, Huiliang inherited the house.

sentences.zh: 例降為公，坐連穆泰罪，失爵，卒。

translations.literal: By precedent he was reduced to duke; implicated in Mu Tai's crime he lost his title and died.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced by precedent to duke, implicated in Mu Tai's affair he lost rank and died.

sentences.zh: 悅字慶宗，歷位豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Yue, styled Qingzong, rose to Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, styled Qingzong, became Inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 時有汝南上蔡董毛奴者，齎錢五千。

translations.literal: At the time there was one Dong Maonu of Shangcai in Runan, carrying five thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In Runan's Shangcai a man named Dong Maonu carried five thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 死于道路。

translations.literal: He died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the road.

sentences.zh: 郡縣人疑張堤為劫，又於堤家得錢五千，堤懼掠，自誣言殺。

translations.literal: The commandery and county people suspected Zhang Di of robbery; at Di's house they also found five thousand cash; Di, fearing torture, falsely confessed to murder.
translations.idiomatic: Locals suspected Zhang Di; five thousand cash was found at his house; fearing torture he confessed murder.

sentences.zh: 至州，悅觀色，疑其不實。

translations.literal: At the province Yue studied his expression and doubted it was true.
translations.idiomatic: At the province Yue read his face and doubted the confession.

sentences.zh: 引見毛奴兄靈之，謂曰：「殺人取錢，當時狼狽，應有所遺，得何物？

translations.literal: He summoned Maonu's elder brother Lingzhi and said: "In killing for money one is flustered at the time and ought to leave something behind—what did you get?
translations.idiomatic: He summoned brother Lingzhi: "A killer in haste leaves something—what was it?

sentences.zh: 」靈之曰：「唯得一刀削。

translations.literal: Lingzhi said: "Only a knife-handle plane.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhi said, "Only a knife-handle plane.

sentences.zh: 」悅取視之，曰：「此非裏巷所為也。

translations.literal: " Yue took it to look and said: "This is not the work of a lane thug.
translations.idiomatic: Yue inspected it: "No alley thug made this.

sentences.zh: 」乃召州內刀匠示之。

translations.literal: He then summoned knife-makers within the province to show it.
translations.idiomatic: He called the province's blade-makers.

sentences.zh: 有郭門前曰：「此刀削，門手所作，去歲賣與郭人董及祖。

translations.literal: One before the Guo Gate said: "This plane was made by the gate artisan; last year it was sold to Guo townsman Dong Jizu.
translations.idiomatic: One at the Guo Gate said a gate artisan made it and sold it last year to Dong Jizu.

sentences.zh: 」悅收及祖詰之，及祖款引。

translations.literal: Yue seized Jizu and interrogated him; Jizu confessed in full.
translations.idiomatic: Yue seized Jizu; he confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 靈之又于及祖身上得毛奴所衣皁襦，及祖伏法。

translations.literal: Lingzhi also found on Jizu's person the black jacket Maonu had worn; Jizu was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: On Jizu Lingzhi found Maonu's black jacket; Jizu was executed.

sentences.zh: 悅察獄，多此類也。

translations.literal: Yue's scrutiny of prisons was often of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's prison work was often thus.

sentences.zh: 俄與鎮南將軍元英攻克義陽，詔改梁司州為郢州，以悅為刺史。

translations.literal: Soon with General Who Pacifies the South Yuan Ying he stormed Yiyang; an edict changed Liang's Si Province to Ying Province and made Yue its inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Soon with Yuan Ying he took Yiyang; Liang's Si became Ying and Yue was made inspector.

sentences.zh: 改為豫州刺史；

translations.literal: Changed to Inspector of Yu Province;
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to Inspector of Yu;

sentences.zh: 論前勳，封漁陽子。

translations.literal: for former merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: for past merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 永平元年，城人白早生謀為叛，遂斬悅首送梁。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongping, the city man Bai Zaosheng plotted rebellion and beheaded Yue's head to send to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping year 1, Bai Zaosheng rebelled and sent Yue's head to Liang.

sentences.zh: 詔揚州移購悅首，贈青州刺史，諡曰莊子。

translations.literal: An edict had Yang Province transfer a reward for Yue's head; he was posthumously made Inspector of Qing, posthumous name Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Province was ordered to ransom the head; posthumously Qing Inspector, posthumous name Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 子朏襲。

translations.literal: Son Fei inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Fei inherited.

sentences.zh: 朏尚宣武妹華陽公主，拜駙馬都尉、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Fei married Emperor Xuanwu's sister Princess Huayang, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards and Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fei wed Princess Huayang, sister of Xuanwu, and became Commandant of Horse Guards and supernumerary attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈滄州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Inspector of Cang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Cang Inspector.

sentences.zh: 子鴻，字慶雲，生粗武。

translations.literal: Son Hong, styled Qingyun, was rough and martial by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Son Hong, styled Qingyun, was rough and martial.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，位都水使者，坐通西魏，賜死。

translations.literal: He inherited the title, held the post of Commissioner of the Imperial Waterways, and was sentenced to death for communicating with Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited, served as Commissioner of Waterways, and was executed for ties to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 子孝政襲。

translations.literal: Son Xiaozheng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xiaozheng inherited.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, by precedent he was reduced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his rank was reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 朏弟裔。

translations.literal: Fei's younger brother Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Fei's younger brother Yi.

sentences.zh: 裔字遵胤，少孤，有志操。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Zunyin, was orphaned young and had resolve and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Zunyin, was orphaned young but steadfast.

sentences.zh: 起家司徒府參軍事，後為員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He began as staff officer in the Minister of State's office, later became Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began in the Minister of State's office, later supernumerary attendant.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，大軍復弘農，乃于溫城送款歸西魏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, when the great army recovered Hongnong, he at Wencheng offered allegiance and returned to Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Datong 3, when Hongnong was recovered, he submitted at Wencheng to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 六年，授北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Inspector of Northern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Year 6 he became Northern Xu Inspector.

sentences.zh: 八年，入朝。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Year 8 he came to court.

sentences.zh: 周文帝嘉之，特蒙賞勞。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou praised him and especially rewarded and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Emperor Wen praised and specially rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 頃之，河內有四千餘家歸附，並裔之鄉舊，乃命領河內郡守，令安集流人。

translations.literal: Before long, more than four thousand households in Henei came over—all Yi's old neighbors—and he was ordered to lead as Administrator of Henei to settle the displaced.
translations.idiomatic: Soon four thousand Henei households, his old neighbors, submitted; he was made Henei magistrate to settle refugees.

sentences.zh: 十五年，周文令山東立義諸將等能率眾入關者，並加重賞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Zhou Wen ordered that righteous leaders east of the mountains who could lead crowds through the Pass would all receive added rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Year 15 Zhou Wen promised added reward to eastern leaders who could bring men through the Pass.

sentences.zh: 裔領戶千室先至，周文欲以封裔。

translations.literal: Yi led a thousand households first to arrive; Zhou Wen wished to enfeoff Yi for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi brought a thousand households first; Wen meant to enfeoff him for it.

sentences.zh: 裔辭曰：「立義之士，遠歸皇化者，皆是其誠心內發，豈裔能率之乎？

translations.literal: Yi declined: "Men who rise in righteousness and return from afar to the imperial transformation all do so from sincere hearts within—how could Yi lead them?
translations.idiomatic: Yi declined: "Righteous men who return from afar act from their own hearts—how could I lead them?

sentences.zh: 今以封裔，便是賣義士以求榮。

translations.literal: To enfeoff Yi now would be to sell righteous men for glory.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffing me now would be buying glory with righteous men.

sentences.zh: 」周文善而從之。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen approved and followed his wish.
translations.idiomatic: Wen approved and let it pass.

sentences.zh: 授帥都督，拜其妻元為襄城郡公主。

translations.literal: He was made Commander-in-Chief and his wife Yuan was made Princess of Xiangcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commander-in-Chief; his wife Yuan became Princess of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，除巴州刺史，進使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵琅邪縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, he was made Inspector of Ba Province, advanced to Commissioner with credentials, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Marshal with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, advanced to Baron of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaomin's accession he was Ba Inspector, then Commissioner, Agile Cavalry Grand General, Grand Marshal equal to the Three Excellencies, Baron of Langye.

sentences.zh: 四年，為禦正中大夫，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Chief Rectifier of the Imperial Clan and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Year 4 he became Chief Rectifier and was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 大軍東討，裔與少師楊舣守軹關，即授懷州刺史。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned east, Yi with Junior Mentor Yang Yi held Zhiguan Pass and at once was made Inspector of Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern campaign Yi with Yang Yi held Zhiguan and was made Huai Inspector.

sentences.zh: 天和初，隨上庸公陸騰討信州反蠻冉令賢等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he followed Duke of Shangyong Lu Teng in attacking the rebellious Man of Xinzhou, Ran Lingxian and others.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianhe's start he followed Duke Lu Teng of Shangyong against Xinzhou rebels Ran Lingxian and others.

sentences.zh: 裔自開州道入，先遣使宣示禍福，群蠻率服。

translations.literal: Yi entered by the Kaizhou route, first sent envoys to proclaim fortune and calamity, and the tribes all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He entered by Kaizhou, proclaimed fortune and ruin, and the tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 曆信、潼二州刺史。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Inspector of Xin and Tong in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Xin and Tong in turn.

sentences.zh: 六年，徵拜大將軍，除西寧州刺史，未及部，卒于京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Grand General and made Inspector of Xining, but before reaching his post he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Year 6 he was summoned Grand General and Xining Inspector but died in the capital before taking post.

sentences.zh: 裔性清約，不事生產，所得俸祿，並散之親戚；

translations.literal: Yi was frugal by nature and did not pursue production; the salary he received he gave entirely to kin;
translations.idiomatic: Yi lived plainly and gave all salary to kin;

sentences.zh: 身死之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: at the day of his death the house had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: at his death the house held nothing.

sentences.zh: 宅宇卑陋，喪庭無所，詔為起祠堂焉。

translations.literal: His dwelling was low and shabby; there was no place for the mourning hall—an edict built a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: His house was mean; no hall for mourning—an edict raised a shrine.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加泗州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumously his former office, with addition of Inspector of Si, posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously his rank plus Si Inspector, posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 子侃嗣。

translations.literal: Son Kan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Kan inherited.

sentences.zh: 侃字道遷，少果勇，未弱冠，便從戎旅。

translations.literal: Kan, styled Daoyuan, was resolute and brave from youth; before the capping age he already followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, styled Daoyuan, was bold young and took the field before capping age.

sentences.zh: 位樂安郡守，以軍功，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He held the post of Administrator of Lean, and for military merit was added Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Marshal with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Lean, and for merit gained Agile Cavalry Grand General and Grand Marshal equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 遷兗州刺史，未之部，卒。

translations.literal: Transferred to Inspector of Yan, he did not reach his post and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shifted to Yan Inspector, he died before arriving.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加豫州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously his former office, with addition of Inspector of Yu, posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously his rank plus Yu Inspector, posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 子運嗣。

translations.literal: Son Yun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yun inherited.

sentences.zh: 金龍弟躍，字寶龍，尚趙郡公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Chuzhi's younger brother Yue, styled Baolong, married the Princess of Zhao Commandery and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Yue, styled Baolong, wed Princess of Zhao and became Commandant of Horse Guards.

sentences.zh: 代兄為雲中鎮將，拜朔州刺史，假安北將軍、河內公。

translations.literal: He replaced his elder brother as commander of the Yunzhong garrison, was made Inspector of Shuo, acting General Who Pacifies the North, and Duke of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced his brother at Yunzhong, became Shuo Inspector, acting General Who Pacifies the North, Duke of Henei.

sentences.zh: 表求罷河西苑封，丐人墾殖。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to abolish the Hexi park preserve and grant the land to people for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to open the Hexi imperial park to settlers.

sentences.zh: 有司執奏，此苑麋鹿所聚，太官取給，若丐人，懼有所闕。

translations.literal: The offices held fast and reported: this park is where elk gather and the Imperial Kitchen draws supply; if granted to people, they feared something would be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Offices objected: elk feed the kitchen; opening it might leave a shortfall.

sentences.zh: 躍固請，孝文從之。

translations.literal: Yue pressed the request firmly; Emperor Xiaowen followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue pressed on; Xiaowen agreed.

sentences.zh: 還為祠部尚書、大鴻臚卿、潁川王師，卒。

translations.literal: Returned as Minister of the Imperial Clan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and tutor to Prince of Yingchuan, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Minister of the Imperial Clan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, tutor to Prince of Yingchuan, then died.

sentences.zh: 楚之父子相繼鎮雲中，朔土服其威德。

translations.literal: Father and son Chuzhi in succession garrisoned Yunzhong; the northern soil submitted to their might and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son held Yunzhong in turn; the north honored their might and virtue.

sentences.zh: 司馬氏桓玄、劉裕之際歸北者，又有司馬景之、叔璠、天助，位並崇顯。

translations.literal: Among the Sima clan who returned north in the time of Huan Xuan and Liu Yu were also Sima Jingzhi, Shufan, and Tianzhu, all holding lofty posts.
translations.idiomatic: Other Simas who fled north in the days of Huan Xuan and Liu Yu—Jingzhi, Shufan, Tianzhu—also rose high.

sentences.zh: 景之字洪略，晉汝南王亮之後。

translations.literal: Jingzhi, styled Honglue, was a descendant of Jin Prince of Runan Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi, styled Honglue, descended from Jin's Prince Liang of Runan.

sentences.zh: 明元時歸闕，賜爵蒼梧公，加征南大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Mingyuan era he came to court, was enfeoffed Duke of Cangwu, and added Grand General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingyuan he came to court, was made Duke of Cangwu and Grand General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 清直有節操。

translations.literal: He was upright and had integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and principled.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈汝南王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 子師子襲爵。

translations.literal: Son Shizi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shizi inherited.

sentences.zh: 景之兄准，字巨之，以泰常末歸魏。

translations.literal: Jingzhi's elder brother Zhun, styled Juzhi, returned to Wei at the end of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Zhun, styled Juzhi, came to Wei late in Taichang.

sentences.zh: 封新安公。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed Duke of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Duke of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 除廣甯太守，改密陵侯。

translations.literal: Made Administrator of Guangning, changed to Marquis of Miling.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Guangning, then was made Marquis of Miling.

sentences.zh: 卒，子安國襲爵。

translations.literal: He died; son Anguo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He died; son Anguo inherited.

sentences.zh: 叔璠，晉安平獻王孚之後。

translations.literal: Shufan was a descendant of Jin Prince of Anping, Duke Xian Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Shufan descended from Jin's Prince Xian Fu of Anping.

sentences.zh: 父曇之，晉河間王。

translations.literal: His father Tanzhi was Jin Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tanzhi was Jin Prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 桓玄、劉裕之際，叔璠與兄國璠奔慕容超。

translations.literal: In the time of Huan Xuan and Liu Yu, Shufan with his elder brother Guo Fan fled to Murong Chao.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil Shufan and brother Guo Fan fled to Murong Chao.

sentences.zh: 後投姚泓。

translations.literal: Later he went to Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 泓滅，奔屈丐。

translations.literal: When Hong was destroyed, he fled to Qu Mugai.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong fell he fled to Qu Mugai.

sentences.zh: 統萬平，兄弟俱入魏。

translations.literal: When Tongwan was pacified, the brothers both entered Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongwan fell both brothers entered Wei.

sentences.zh: 國璠賜爵淮南公，叔璠賜爵丹楊侯。

translations.literal: Guo Fan was enfeoffed Duke of Huainan; Shufan was enfeoffed Marquis of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Fan became Duke of Huainan; Shufan Marquis of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 天助，自雲晉驃騎將軍元顯之子。

translations.literal: Tianzhu was himself son of Jin General of Agile Cavalry Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhu was son of Jin's Agile Cavalry General Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 歸闕，封東海公，曆青、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: Coming to court, he was enfeoffed Duke of Donghai and held the posts of Inspector of Qing and Yan in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was Duke of Donghai and dual Inspector of Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 昶好犬馬，愛武事。

translations.literal: Chang loved dogs and horses and delighted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chang loved hounds and horses and delighted in arms.

sentences.zh: 入魏曆紀，猶布衣皁冠，同凶素之服。

translations.literal: Having entered Wei and passed through several reigns, he still wore plain cloth and black cap, the same garb as for fierce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei through several reigns he still wore plain cloth and black cap like mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 然呵罵僮僕，音雜夷夏。

translations.literal: Yet he would shout at and beat servants; his speech mixed barbarian and Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he abused servants in a mixed barbarian-Chinese tongue.

sentences.zh: 雖在公坐，諸王每侮弄之。

translations.literal: Even in public sessions the princes would each mock and toy with him.
translations.idiomatic: Even in open court the princes mocked him.

sentences.zh: 或戾手齧臂，至於痛傷，笑呼之聲，聞於御聽。

translations.literal: Some would twist his hand and bite his arm until he was wounded in pain; the sound of their laughter reached the emperor's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Some twisted his hand or bit his arm till he cried; laughter reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 孝文每優假之，不以怪問。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen always treated him with extra favor and did not regard it as strange to question.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen always indulged him and never took offense.

sentences.zh: 至於陳奏本國事故，語及征役，則斂容涕泗，悲動左右。

translations.literal: But when he memorialized on affairs of his native state and spoke of levies and corvée, he would compose his face and weep; grief moved those beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet memorializing on his old country and corvée he wept till all beside him grieved.

sentences.zh: 而天性褊躁，喜怒不恆。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was narrow and quick; joy and anger were not constant.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was narrow and volatile.

sentences.zh: 每至威忿，楚撲特苦；

translations.literal: Whenever wrath flared, the cudgel and switch were especially harsh;
translations.idiomatic: In rage his beatings were savage;

sentences.zh: 引待南士，禮多不足。

translations.literal: toward southern gentlemen his courtesy was often lacking.
translations.idiomatic: toward southerners his courtesy often failed.

sentences.zh: 緣此，人懷畏避。

translations.literal: Because of this, men harbored fear and kept away.
translations.idiomatic: Men feared him and kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 太和初，轉內都坐大官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was transferred to Director of the Inner Court's Grand Provisioners.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe he became Director of the Inner Court's Grand Provisioners.

sentences.zh: 及齊初，詔昶與諸將南伐。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi an edict had Chang and the generals campaign south.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi's founding Chang was ordered south with the generals.

sentences.zh: 路經徐州，哭拜其母舊堂，哀感從者。

translations.literal: Passing Xuzhou, he wept and bowed at his mother's old hall; grief moved those who followed.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou he wept at his mother's old hall and moved his escort.

sentences.zh: 乃遍循故居，處處隕涕，左右亦莫不酸鼻。

translations.literal: He then went everywhere through his old dwellings; at each place tears fell, and those beside him could not keep from stinging in the nose.
translations.idiomatic: He walked his old streets weeping; companions wept with him.

sentences.zh: 及至軍所，將臨陣，四面拜諸將士，自陳家國滅亡，蒙朝廷慈覆。

translations.literal: When he reached the army's place and was about to take the field, he bowed on four sides to the officers and soldiers and himself declared that his house and state were destroyed and he was covered by the court's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Before battle he bowed to the ranks, saying his state was gone and only the court's grace remained.

sentences.zh: 辭理切至，聲氣激揚，涕泗橫流，三軍咸為感歎。

translations.literal: His words were cutting and true, his voice excited and rising; tears streamed; the whole army was moved to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: His words were keen, his voice fierce; tears ran; the whole army sighed.

sentences.zh: 後昶恐水雨方降，表請還師，從之。

translations.literal: Later Chang, fearing that rain would soon come, memorialized asking to withdraw the army, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Later, fearing rain, he asked to withdraw and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 又加儀同三司，領儀曹尚書。

translations.literal: Again added Grand Marshal with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies and head of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was again Grand Marshal equal to the Three Excellencies and head of Rites.

sentences.zh: 于時改革朝儀，詔昶與蔣少遊專主其事。

translations.literal: At the time the court was reforming court ceremony; an edict had Chang and Jiang Shaoyou take sole charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The court reformed ritual; Chang and Jiang Shaoyou were put in sole charge.

sentences.zh: 昶條上舊式，略不遺忘。

translations.literal: Chang listed the old forms upward; scarcely anything was forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Chang listed the old forms and forgot almost nothing.

sentences.zh: 孝文臨宣文堂，引武興王楊集始入宴，詔昶曰：「集始，邊方之酋，不足以當諸侯之禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen at the Xuanwen Hall summoned Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi to enter the feast and told Chang: "Jishi is a frontier chieftain—not enough to match the rites due feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanwen Hall Xiaowen feasted Prince Yang Jishi of Wuxing and told Chang, "A frontier chief cannot match feudal rites—yet the throne does not disdain small states' ministers, so we trouble you nobles here.

sentences.zh: 但王者不遺小國之臣，故勞公卿於此。

translations.literal: Yet the king does not disdain the minister of a small state, and therefore has wearied you, duke and ministers, here.
translations.idiomatic: That is why you are wearied here.

sentences.zh: 」又為中書監。

translations.literal: Again made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was again Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開建五等，封昶齊郡公，加宋王之號。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, Chang was enfeoffed Duke of Qi Commandery with the added title of King of Song.
translations.idiomatic: When five ranks were founded he was Duke of Qi Commandery with the added title King of Song.

sentences.zh: 十七年，孝文臨經武殿，大議南伐。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Xiaowen at the Jingwu Hall held great discussion of the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Year 17 Xiaowen at Jingwu Hall debated the southern war.

sentences.zh: 語及劉、蕭篡奪之事，昶每悲泣不已。

translations.literal: When talk touched the usurpations of Liu and Xiao, Chang would weep without end.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of Liu and Xiao usurpations he wept without cease.

sentences.zh: 帝亦為之流涕，禮之彌崇。

translations.literal: The emperor also wept for it; his courtesy toward Chang grew ever more exalted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept too and honored him the more.

sentences.zh: 十八年，除使持節、都督吳越楚彭城諸軍事、大將軍、開府，鎮徐州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was made Commissioner with credentials, Area Commander of Wu, Yue, Chu, and Pengcheng forces, Grand General, and Grand Marshal, garrisoning Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Year 18 he was Commissioner, area commander of Wu, Yue, Chu, and Pengcheng, Grand General and Grand Marshal at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 昶頻表辭大將軍，詔不許。

translations.literal: Chang repeatedly memorialized declining the post of Grand General; the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly declined Grand General; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 及發，帝親餞之，命百寮賦詩贈昶。

translations.literal: At his departure the emperor personally saw him off and ordered the hundred officials to compose poems to present to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: At departure the emperor feasted him and ordered poems from the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 又以其文集一部賜昶。

translations.literal: He also gave him one collection of his own writings.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave a volume of his own writings.

sentences.zh: 帝因以所制文筆示之曰：「時契勝殘，事鐘文業。

translations.literal: The emperor then showed him the brushwork he himself had composed and said: "The times fit ending slaughter; affairs turn on literary enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed his own writing and said, "Times favor ending slaughter; affairs turn on letters.

sentences.zh: 雖則不學，欲罷不能。

translations.literal: Though I do not study, I cannot bear to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Though I do not study, I cannot stop.

sentences.zh: 脫思一見，故以相示，雖無足味，聊復為一笑耳。

translations.literal: On a whim I wished you to see them, and therefore show them—though they have no flavor worth speaking of, they may still raise a laugh.
translations.idiomatic: I wished you to see them—thin fare, but perhaps a laugh.

sentences.zh: 」其重昶如是。

translations.literal: He valued Chang to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: He valued Chang to that degree.

sentences.zh: 自昶背彭城，至是久矣，昔齋宇山池，並尚存立；

translations.literal: From the time Chang left Pengcheng until now was long; his former fasting halls, mountains, and pools still stood;
translations.idiomatic: Long since he left Pengcheng his old halls, hills, and pools still stood;

sentences.zh: 昶更修繕，還處其中。

translations.literal: Chang repaired them anew and dwelt within them again.
translations.idiomatic: Chang restored them and lived there again.

sentences.zh: 不能綏邊懷物，撫接義故，而閨門喧猥，內外奸雜，舊吏莫不慨歎。

translations.literal: He could not soothe the frontier and cherish men, comfort and receive old associates, yet within the inner gates it was noisy and vulgar, inside and outside mixed with villainy, and old officials all sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the border and old friends while his household grew riotous and corrupt; veterans sighed.

sentences.zh: 預營墓于彭城西南，與三公主同塋而異穴。

translations.literal: He prepared his tomb southwest of Pengcheng, in the same mound as the Third Princess but in a separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared a tomb southwest of Pengcheng, sharing a mound with the Third Princess but not her vault.

sentences.zh: 發石累之，墳崩，壓殺十餘人。

translations.literal: When stone was piled the mound collapsed and crushed more than ten men to death.
translations.idiomatic: While piling stone the mound collapsed and killed more than ten.

sentences.zh: 後復移改，公私費害。

translations.literal: Later it was moved and altered again; public and private expense was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was moved again at great public and private cost.

sentences.zh: 昶嫡子承緒，主所生也。

translations.literal: Chang's eldest son Chengxu was born of the princess, his principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Chengxu was the princess's child.

sentences.zh: 少而尪疾，尚孝文妹彭城長公主，為駙馬都尉，先昶卒。

translations.literal: Sickly from youth, he married Emperor Xiaowen's sister Princess of Pengcheng, was Commandant of Horse Guards, and died before Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Frail from youth, he wed Xiaowen's sister Princess of Pengcheng, was Commandant of Horse Guards, and predeceased Chang.

sentences.zh: 承緒子暉，字重昌，為世子，襲封。

translations.literal: Chengxu's son Hui, styled Chongchang, was heir and inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxu's son Hui, styled Chongchang, was heir and inherited.

sentences.zh: 尚宣武第二姊蘭陵長公主。

translations.literal: He married Emperor Xuanwu's second elder sister Princess of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He married Xuanwu's second elder sister, Princess of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 主嚴妒，暉嘗私幸主侍婢。

translations.literal: The princess was fiercely jealous; Hui once secretly favored her waiting maid.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was fiercely jealous; Hui once lay with her maid.

sentences.zh: 有身，主笞殺之；

translations.literal: She became pregnant; the princess flogged her to death;
translations.idiomatic: The maid conceived; the princess beat her dead;

sentences.zh: 剖其孕子，節解，以草裝實婢腹，裸以示暉。

translations.literal: cut open the pregnancy, dismembered it limb by limb, stuffed the maid's belly with straw, and displayed her naked to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: she cut out the child, dismembered it, stuffed straw in the maid's belly, and showed the corpse naked to Hui.

sentences.zh: 暉遂忿憾，疏薄公主。

translations.literal: Hui then nursed resentment and grew cold toward the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Hui nursed hatred and grew cold toward her.

sentences.zh: 公主姊因入聽講，言其故于靈太后。

translations.literal: The princess's elder sister, entering to hear lectures, told Empress Dowager Ling the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister, attending lectures at court, told Empress Dowager Ling.

sentences.zh: 太后敕清河王懌窮其事。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered Prince of Qinghe Yi to investigate the affair to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered Prince Yi of Qinghe to investigate.

sentences.zh: 懌與高陽王雍、廣平王懷奏其不和狀，請離婚，削除封位。

translations.literal: Yi with Prince of Gaoyang Yong and Prince of Guangping Huai memorialized their disharmony and asked divorce and removal of enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Yi with Prince Yong of Gaoyang and Prince Huai of Guangping reported their strife and sought divorce and loss of rank.

sentences.zh: 太后從之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed.

sentences.zh: 公主在宮內周歲，雍等屢請聽復舊義。

translations.literal: The princess was in the palace a full year; Yong and the others repeatedly asked permission to restore the old bond.
translations.idiomatic: A year in the palace Yong and others repeatedly asked to restore the marriage.

sentences.zh: 太后流涕送公主，誡令謹敕。

translations.literal: The empress dowager wept as she sent the princess back and admonished her to be cautious and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wept sending her back and warned her to be restrained.

sentences.zh: 正光初，暉又私淫張、陳二氏女。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang Hui again secretly debauched the daughters of the Zhang and Chen families.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengguang Hui again lay secretly with daughters of Zhang and Chen.

sentences.zh: 公主更不檢忌。

translations.literal: The princess no longer checked or forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: The princess no longer restrained him.

sentences.zh: 主姑陳留公主共將扇獎，與暉復致忿諍。

translations.literal: The princess's aunt Princess of Chenliu together wielded fans to encourage them, and with Hui again came to angry quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: Her aunt Princess of Chenliu fanned the affair on, and Hui quarreled with the princess again.

sentences.zh: 暉推主墜床，手腳毆蹈，主遂傷胎。

translations.literal: Hui pushed the princess from the bed and beat and trampled her hands and feet; the princess thus miscarried.
translations.idiomatic: Hui threw her from the bed and trampled her; she miscarried.

sentences.zh: 暉懼罪逃逸。

translations.literal: Hui, fearing punishment, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, Hui fled.

sentences.zh: 靈太后召清河王懌決其事。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling summoned Prince of Qinghe Yi to decide the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling summoned Prince Yi of Qinghe to judge.

sentences.zh: 二家女髡笞會宮，兄弟皆坐鞭刑。

translations.literal: The two families' daughters were shaved and flogged at the palace assembly; the brothers were all punished with the whip.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang and Chen daughters were shaved and flogged at court; their brothers were whipped.

sentences.zh: 徙配敦煌為兵。

translations.literal: They were banished to Dunhuang as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: They were sent to Dunhuang as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 主因傷致薨，太后親臨慟哭，舉哀太極東堂。

translations.literal: The princess died from her wounds; the empress dowager came in person to mourn and weep, and mourning was raised at the eastern hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: The princess died of her wounds; the empress dowager mourned at the eastern hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 出葬城西，太后親送數里，盡哀而還。

translations.literal: Burial was outside the western wall; the empress dowager escorted several li and returned only when grief was spent.
translations.idiomatic: Buried outside the west wall; the empress dowager escorted her several li and returned in grief.

sentences.zh: 後執暉于河內溫縣，幽于司州，將加死刑。

translations.literal: Later Hui was seized at Wen in Henei, imprisoned in Si Province, and was to receive the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hui was taken at Wen in Henei, held in Si Province, and marked for death.

sentences.zh: 會赦，免。

translations.literal: An amnesty came and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 後復其官爵，遷征虜將軍、中散大夫，卒，家遂衰頓。

translations.literal: Later his office and title were restored; he was moved to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Regular Attendant, and died—the house then declined.
translations.idiomatic: Later rank was restored; he was General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Regular Attendant, then died—the house faded.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤，字智亮，齊明帝第六子，廢主寶卷之母弟也。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin, styled Zhiliang, was the sixth son of Emperor Ming of Qi, younger brother of the mother of the deposed emperor Baojuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin, styled Zhiliang, was Qi Emperor Ming's sixth son, younger brother of deposed Emperor Baojuan's mother.

sentences.zh: 在齊封建安王。

translations.literal: In Qi he was enfeoffed Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he was Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 及和帝立，改封鄱陽王。

translations.literal: When Emperor He of Qi took the throne, he was changed to Prince of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He acceded he was made Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 梁武克建業，以兵守之，將加害焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang took Jiankang, troops guarded him and were about to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Wu took Jiankang, guards were set to kill him.

sentences.zh: 其家閹人顏文智與左右麻拱、黃神密計，穿牆夜出寶夤。

translations.literal: His household eunuch Yan Wenzhi with attendants Ma Gong and Huang Shen secretly plotted, broke through the wall by night, and brought Baoyin out.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Yan Wenzhi with Ma Gong and Huang Shen broke through the wall at night and stole him out.

sentences.zh: 具小船於江岸，脫本衣服，著烏布襦；

translations.literal: They prepared a small boat on the riverbank; they stripped his formal dress and put on a black cloth jacket;
translations.idiomatic: A small boat waited on the bank; they stripped his robes for a black cloth jacket;

sentences.zh: 腰系千許錢，潛赴江畔；

translations.literal: at the waist he tied more than a thousand cash and stole to the riverbank;
translations.idiomatic: he tied a thousand-odd cash at his waist and stole to the shore;

sentences.zh: 躡屩徒步，腳無全皮。

translations.literal: treading sandals he went on foot; his feet had no whole skin.
translations.idiomatic: in sandals he walked until his feet had no whole skin.

sentences.zh: 防守者至明追之。

translations.literal: The guards pursued at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Guards pursued at dawn.

sentences.zh: 寶夤假為釣者，隨流上下十餘里，追者不疑。

translations.literal: Baoyin pretended to be a fisherman, drifting up and down the stream more than ten li; the pursuers did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: He played fisherman, drifting ten li; pursuers passed him by.

sentences.zh: 待散，乃度西岸。

translations.literal: When they dispersed, he then crossed to the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: When they broke off he crossed to the west bank.

sentences.zh: 遂委命投華文榮。

translations.literal: He then entrusted his life to Hua Wenrong.
translations.idiomatic: He then cast himself on Hua Wenrong.

sentences.zh: 文榮與其從天龍、惠連等三人，棄家，將寶夤遁匿山澗，賃驢乘之，晝伏宵行。

translations.literal: Wenrong with his followers Tianlong, Huilian, and three others abandoned their families, hid Baoyin in mountain ravines, hired donkeys to ride, lay by day and marched by night.
translations.idiomatic: Wenrong with Tianlong, Huilian, and three others abandoned home, hid him in the hills, rode hired donkeys, and marched by night.

sentences.zh: 景明二年，至壽春東城戍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingming he reached the eastern-wall garrison of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingming year 2 he reached Shouyang's eastern garrison.

sentences.zh: 戍主杜元倫推檢，知實蕭氏子，以禮延待。

translations.literal: Garrison chief Du Yuanlun examined him and knew he was truly a son of the Xiao house; he received him with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison chief Du Yuanlun identified a true Xiao prince and received him with ceremony.

sentences.zh: 馳告揚州刺史、任城王澄。

translations.literal: He sent word in haste to Yang Province Inspector, Prince of Rencheng Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He reported at once to Yang Inspector Prince Cheng of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 澄以車馬侍衛迎之。

translations.literal: Cheng came with carriage, horses, and guards to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng came with carriage, horses, and escort.

sentences.zh: 時年十六，徒步憔悴，見者以為掠賣生口也。

translations.literal: He was then sixteen; on foot, haggard and worn, viewers thought him a kidnapped slave being sold.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen, on foot and haggard, onlookers took him for a sold captive.

sentences.zh: 澄待以客禮。

translations.literal: Cheng received him with guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng treated him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 乃請喪君斬衰之服，澄遣人曉示情禮，以喪兄之制，給其齊衰，寶夤從命。

translations.literal: He then asked for the hemp mourning of a murdered lord; Cheng sent men to explain the proper feeling and ritual, and in the rites for a murdered elder brother gave him the hemp of the next degree; Baoyin obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for hemp mourning for a slain sovereign; Cheng explained ritual and gave him second-degree hemp for a slain elder brother; Baoyin obeyed.

sentences.zh: 澄率官僚赴吊。

translations.literal: Cheng led the officials to offer condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng led officials to mourn.

sentences.zh: 寶夤居處有禮，不飲酒食肉；

translations.literal: Baoyin's dwelling had ritual propriety; he did not drink wine or eat meat;
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin lived with ritual; no wine or meat;

sentences.zh: 輟笑簡言，一同極哀之節。

translations.literal: he ceased laughter and spoke briefly, all one with the utmost of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: he ceased laughter and spoke little, in utmost mourning.

sentences.zh: 壽春多其故義，皆受慰唁。

translations.literal: In Shouyang many of his old associates came; all received his comfort and condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Many old associates in Shouyang came; he received them in mourning.

sentences.zh: 唯不見夏侯一族，以其同梁故也。

translations.literal: Only he did not see the Xiahou clan, because they were of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He avoided the Xiahous, being Liang men.

sentences.zh: 改日造澄，澄深器重之。

translations.literal: Another day he visited Cheng; Cheng deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he called on Cheng, who prized him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及至京師，宣武禮之甚重。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, Emperor Xuanwu honored him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Xuanwu honored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 伏訴闕下，請兵南伐，雖遇暴風大雨，終不暫移。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself below the palace gate and begged troops for a southern campaign; though violent wind and heavy rain came, he never moved for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt at the gate begging troops south; through storm he did not stir.

sentences.zh: 是年，梁江州刺史陳伯之與其長史褚胄等自壽春歸降，請軍立效。

translations.literal: That year Liang's Inspector of Jiangzhou Chen Bozhi with his chief clerk Chu Zhou and others returned from Shouyang to surrender and asked to lead an army for merit.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liang's Jiang Inspector Chen Bozhi with Chu Zhou surrendered from Shouyang offering service.

sentences.zh: 帝謂伯之所陳，時不可失。

translations.literal: The emperor said that what Bozhi reported could not be lost in time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Bozhi's offer could not wait.

sentences.zh: 以寶夤懇誠，除使持節、都督、東揚州刺史、鎮東將軍、丹楊郡公、齊王，配兵一萬，令據東城，待秋冬大舉。

translations.literal: Because Baoyin was earnest and sincere, he was made Commissioner with credentials, Area Commander, Inspector of Eastern Yang, General Who Pacifies the East, Duke of Danyang, Prince of Qi, with ten thousand troops assigned, ordered to hold the eastern wall and await the great stroke in autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: For his earnestness he was Commissioner, eastern commander, Eastern Yang Inspector, General Who Pacifies the East, Duke of Danyang, Prince of Qi, with ten thousand men at the eastern wall till autumn's campaign.

sentences.zh: 寶夤明當拜命，其夜慟哭。

translations.literal: The night before he was to receive the appointment he wept in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: The night before investiture he wept in anguish.

sentences.zh: 至晨，備禮策授，賜車馬什物，事從豐厚，猶不及劉昶之優隆也。

translations.literal: At dawn the full ritual of investiture was prepared; carriage, horses, and objects were granted; the affair was rich and thick, yet still not equal to Liu Chang's exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn full investiture came with rich gifts—yet still short of Liu Chang's favor.

sentences.zh: 又任其募天下壯勇，得數千人。

translations.literal: He was also allowed to recruit valiant men throughout the realm and got several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He was allowed to recruit braves and gathered thousands.

sentences.zh: 以文智等三人為積弩將軍，文榮等三人為強弩將軍，並為軍主。

translations.literal: Wenzhi and the other three were made generals of powerful crossbows; Wenrong and the other three were made generals of strong crossbows, all as army commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhi's three became powerful-crossbow generals; Wenrong's three strong-crossbow generals—all army commanders.

sentences.zh: 寶夤雖少羈寓，而志性雅重。

translations.literal: Though Baoyin was young and long a hostage, his will and nature were elegant and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Young and long exiled, his will was still elegant and grave.

sentences.zh: 過期猶絕酒肉，慘悴形色，蔬食粗衣，未嘗嬉笑。

translations.literal: Past the mourning term he still abstained from wine and meat; his face was haggard, he ate vegetables and coarse cloth and never laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Past mourning he still abstained; haggard, in vegetables and coarse cloth, he never laughed.

sentences.zh: 及被命當南伐，貴要多相憑托，門庭賓客若市。

translations.literal: When ordered to campaign south, the great and powerful relied on him in multitudes; his gate was like a market of guests.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered south, the powerful crowded his gate like a market.

sentences.zh: 而書記相尋，寶夤接對報復，不失其理。

translations.literal: Yet letters followed one another and Baoyin answered and replied without losing reason.
translations.idiomatic: Letters piled up; he answered each without losing reason.

sentences.zh: 正始元年，寶夤行達汝陰，東城已陷，遂停壽春之棲賢寺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengshi, Baoyin reached Ruyin; the eastern wall had fallen, so he stopped at Shouyang's Qixian Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengshi year 1 he reached Ruyin; the eastern wall had fallen, so he halted at Shouyang's Qixian Temple.

sentences.zh: 逢梁將姜慶真內侵，圍逼壽春。

translations.literal: He met Liang general Jiang Qingzhen invading within; Qingzhen besieged Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Jiang Qingzhen invaded and besieged Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 寶夤率眾力戰，破走之。

translations.literal: Baoyin led the crowd in fierce battle and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin fought hard and routed him.

sentences.zh: 寶夤勇冠諸軍，聞見者莫不壯之。

translations.literal: Baoyin's courage topped the armies; those who heard and saw were all stirred.
translations.idiomatic: His courage topped the armies; all who saw were stirred.

sentences.zh: 還，改封梁郡公。

translations.literal: On return he was changed to Duke of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made Duke of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及中山王英南伐，寶夤又表求征。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhongshan Ying campaigned south, Baoyin again memorialized asking to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ying of Zhongshan marched south Baoyin again asked to go.

sentences.zh: 與英頻破梁軍，乘勝攻鐘離。

translations.literal: With Ying he repeatedly defeated Liang armies and pressed the attack on Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: With Ying he repeatedly beat Liang and pressed Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 淮水泛溢，寶夤與英狼狽引退，士卒死沒者十四五。

translations.literal: The Huai overflowed; Baoyin and Ying withdrew in disorder; soldiers drowned and perished—four or five in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai flooded; Baoyin and Ying fled in disorder; four or five in ten drowned.

sentences.zh: 有司奏處以極法。

translations.literal: The offices memorialized that he should receive the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Offices asked the extreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 詔恕死，免官削爵還第。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned death; he was dismissed from office, stripped of title, and returned to his house.
translations.idiomatic: An edict spared death, stripped office and rank, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 尋尚南陽長公主。

translations.literal: Soon he married the Princess of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he married the Princess of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 公主有婦德，寶夤盡雍和之禮，雖好合而敬事不替。

translations.literal: The princess had wifely virtue; Baoyin fully observed harmonious rites; though fond of her, his respectful service did not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was virtuous; he kept full harmony; fond yet never slack in respect.

sentences.zh: 寶夤每入室，公主必立以待之，相遇如賓，自非太妃疾篤，未曾歸休。

translations.literal: Whenever Baoyin entered the chamber the princess always stood to await him; they met like guests; unless the queen mother's illness was grave he never retired to rest.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered she stood; they met as guests; unless the queen mother was gravely ill he never rested within.

sentences.zh: 寶夤器性溫順，自處以禮，奉敬公主，內外庇穆。

translations.literal: Baoyin's disposition was gentle and compliant; he placed himself within ritual, revered the princess, and inside and outside were sheltered in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and compliant, he kept ritual, revered her, and household and court were at peace.

sentences.zh: 清河王懌親而重之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qinghe Yi was kin and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Qinghe was kin and prized him.

sentences.zh: 永平四年，盧昶克梁朐山戍，以琅邪戍主傅文驥守之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongping, Lu Chang took Liang's Zhushan garrison; Langye garrison chief Fu Wenji guarded it.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping year 4 Lu Chang took Liang's Zhushan; Langye chief Fu Wenji held it.

sentences.zh: 梁師攻文驥，昶督眾軍救之。

translations.literal: Liang's army attacked Wenji; Chang supervised the mass of armies to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang attacked Wenji; Chang led the host to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 詔寶夤為使持節、假安南將軍，別將長驅往赴，受昶節度。

translations.literal: An edict made Baoyin Commissioner with credentials and acting General Who Pacifies the South, a separate commander driving deep to the rescue, under Chang's command.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was Commissioner and acting General Who Pacifies the South, a separate column under Chang.

sentences.zh: 寶夤受詔，泣涕橫流，哽咽良久。

translations.literal: Receiving the edict, tears streamed; he choked for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the edict he wept and choked long.

sentences.zh: 後昶軍敗，唯寶夤全師而還。

translations.literal: Later Chang's army was defeated; only Baoyin brought the whole army back intact.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chang was beaten; only Baoyin brought the army back whole.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，除瀛州刺史，復其齊王，遷冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanxi he was made Inspector of Ying, restored as Prince of Qi, and moved to Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi's start made him Ying Inspector, restored Prince of Qi, then Ji Inspector.

sentences.zh: 及大乘賊起，寶夤遣軍討之，頻為賊破。

translations.literal: When the Mahayana rebels rose, Baoyin sent troops to attack them and was repeatedly beaten by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Mahayana rebels rose he sent troops and was repeatedly beaten.

sentences.zh: 台軍至，乃滅之。

translations.literal: When the capital army arrived, they were then destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital army came they were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，還京師。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling held court and he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling held court; he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 梁將康絢於浮山堰淮以灌揚、徐。

translations.literal: Liang general Kang Xuan at Fushan dammed the Huai to flood Yang and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Kang Xuan dammed the Huai at Fushan to flood Yang and Xu.

sentences.zh: 除寶夤使持節、都督東討軍事、鎮東將軍以討之，復封梁郡公。

translations.literal: Baoyin was made Commissioner with credentials, Area Commander of the Eastern Expedition, General Who Pacifies the East, to attack him, and again enfeoffed Duke of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was eastern commander and General Who Pacifies the East against him, again Duke of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，梁堰既成，淮水將為揚、徐之患，寶夤乃於堰上流更鑿新渠，水乃小減。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping, when Liang's dam was complete and the Huai was about to become a calamity for Yang and Xu, Baoyin cut a new channel above the dam and the water lessened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiping's start: Liang's dam threatened Yang and Xu; Baoyin cut a channel above it and eased the flood.

sentences.zh: 乃遣壯士千餘人夜度淮，燒其竹木營聚，破其三壘，火數日不滅。

translations.literal: He then sent more than a thousand stalwarts by night across the Huai, burned their bamboo-and-wood camps, broke three fortresses, and fires burned for days without going out.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a thousand men by night across the Huai, burned bamboo camps, broke three forts; fires burned for days.

sentences.zh: 又分遣將破梁將垣孟孫、張僧副等於淮北。

translations.literal: He also sent separate commanders to defeat Liang generals Yuan Mengsun and Zhang Sengfu north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Separate columns defeated Liang generals Yuan Mengsun and Zhang Sengfu north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 仍度淮南，焚梁徐州刺史張豹子等十一營。

translations.literal: He then crossed south of the Huai and burned eleven camps of Liang's Inspector of Xuzhou Zhang Baozi and others.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed south and burned eleven camps of Liang's Xu Inspector Zhang Baozi and others.

sentences.zh: 及還京師，為殿中尚書。

translations.literal: On return to the capital he was made Director of the Palace Department.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was Director of the Palace Department.

sentences.zh: 寶夤之在淮堰，梁武寓書招誘之。

translations.literal: While Baoyin was at the Huai dam, Emperor Wu of Liang sent a letter lodged to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: At the Huai dam Liang's Emperor Wu sent a letter to entice him.

sentences.zh: 寶夤表送其書，陳其忿毒之意。

translations.literal: Baoyin memorialized forwarding the letter and stated his bitter, poisonous intent.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin forwarded the letter and declared his bitter resolve.

sentences.zh: 志存雪復，屢請居邊。

translations.literal: His will was set on wiping away shame; he repeatedly asked to dwell on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His heart was vengeance; he repeatedly asked the border.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，為都督、徐州刺史、車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era he was Area Commander and Inspector of Xuzhou and Grand General of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengui he was Xuzhou commander and Grand General of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 乃起學館於清東，朔望引見土姓子弟，接以恩顏，與論經義。

translations.literal: He then raised a school east of Qing, and on the first and fifteenth of the month summoned local gentry's sons, received them with kind face, and discussed the classics with them.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a school east of Qing and on the first and fifteenth summoned local sons to discuss the classics.

sentences.zh: 勤於聽理，吏人愛之。

translations.literal: Diligent in hearing cases, clerks and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent in judgment, clerks and people loved him.

sentences.zh: 正光二年，徵為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengguang he was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengguang year 2 he was summoned as Left Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 善於吏職，甚有聲名。

translations.literal: Skilled in clerical duty, he had a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in office work, he won great fame.

sentences.zh: 四年，上表曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he memorialized:

sentences.zh: 竊惟文武之名，在人之極地；

translations.literal: I reflect that the names civil and martial stand at the utmost of men;
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that civil and martial names stand at men's utmost;

sentences.zh: 德行之稱，為生之最首。

translations.literal: the title of virtue and conduct is the foremost of life.
translations.idiomatic: virtue and conduct are life's foremost titles.

sentences.zh: 忠貞之美，立朝之譽；

translations.literal: The beauty of loyalty and integrity is the praise of standing at court;
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and integrity are praise at court;

sentences.zh: 仁義之號，處身之端。

translations.literal: the name of benevolence and righteousness is the beginning of comporting oneself.
translations.idiomatic: benevolence and righteousness begin personal conduct.

sentences.zh: 自非職惟九官，任當四嶽，授曰爾諧，讓稱俞往，將何以克厭大名，允茲令問。

translations.literal: Unless one's office is among the nine ministers and one's charge is the four mountains, with appointment saying "you shall harmonize" and yielding called "we go," how can one bear the great name and fulfill this fine repute?
translations.idiomatic: Unless one holds the nine ministries or the four mountains' charge—with "you shall harmonize" in appointment and "we go" in yielding—how bear the great name and fulfill fine repute?

sentences.zh: 自比以來，官罔高卑，人無貴賤，皆飾辭假說，用相褒舉。

translations.literal: From recent times, office knows no high or low, man knows no noble or base—all adorn words with borrowed talk and use it to praise and lift one another.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, high or low, noble or base—all polish borrowed phrases to praise each other.

sentences.zh: 求者不能量其多少，與者不能核其是非，遂使冠履相貿，名實皆爽。

translations.literal: Those who ask cannot measure how much; those who give cannot verify right and wrong; thus cap and shoe are traded, name and reality both lost.
translations.idiomatic: Givers cannot verify truth; caps and shoes trade places; name and fact both fail.

sentences.zh: 謂之考功，事同泛陟，紛紛漫漫，焉可勝言！

translations.literal: Calling it examination of merit, the affair is like indiscriminate promotion—confused and boundless, how can it be told!
translations.idiomatic: Merit review becomes indiscriminate promotion—endless confusion, beyond telling!

sentences.zh: 又在京之官，積年十考。

translations.literal: Again, officials in the capital accumulate ten years of examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Again, capital officials pile ten years of reviews.

sentences.zh: 其中，或所事之主，遷移數四；

translations.literal: Among them, some have had masters they served shift three or four times;
translations.idiomatic: Some have served masters who shifted three or four times;

sentences.zh: 或所奉之君，身亡廢絕。

translations.literal: Or the lord they served had died or been deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Or the lord they served was dead or deposed.

sentences.zh: 雖當時文簿，記其殿最，日久月遙，散落都盡。

translations.literal: Though the documents of the time recorded their grades, as months and years passed everything was scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Records of the day were lost over the years.

sentences.zh: 累年之後，方求追訪，無不苟相悅附，共為脣齒；

translations.literal: Only after many years would they seek to trace matters back; none failed to curry favor with one another and act as lip and teeth;
translations.idiomatic: Years later, when records were sought back, everyone flattered one another like allies;

sentences.zh: 飾垢掩疵，妄加丹素，趣令得階而已，無所顧惜。

translations.literal: they covered stains and hid flaws, recklessly applied vermilion and white, only aiming to gain a step in rank, with no regard for anything else.
translations.idiomatic: they whitewashed faults and pushed promotions, caring only for rank.

sentences.zh: 賢達君子，未免斯患；

translations.literal: Even worthy and eminent gentlemen could not escape this affliction;
translations.idiomatic: Even the worthy were not spared;

sentences.zh: 中庸已降，夫復何論！

translations.literal: for those below the middling, what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: for lesser men, needless to say.

sentences.zh: 官以求成，身以請立，上下相蒙，莫斯為甚。

translations.literal: Office was sought to complete one's aims, the person to secure one's standing—superior and inferior deceived one another; nothing exceeded this.
translations.idiomatic: Men sought posts to finish their aims and bodies to secure standing; deceit between ranks was worst of all.

sentences.zh: 又勤恤人隱，咸歸守令，厥任非輕，所責實重。

translations.literal: Moreover, in diligently caring for the people's hidden woes, all responsibility fell on prefects and magistrates; their charge was not light and what was required of them was truly weighty.
translations.idiomatic: People's grievances rested on local magistrates, whose burden was heavy.

sentences.zh: 然及其考課，悉以六載為約，既而限滿代還，復經六年而敘。

translations.literal: Yet when it came to their examination, all were bound by a six-year term; when the term expired they were replaced and returned, and only after another six years was advancement granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their review used a six-year term, then six more years before promotion.

sentences.zh: 是則歲周十二，始得一階。

translations.literal: Thus twelve years had to pass before one gained a single rank.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years passed for one rank.

sentences.zh: 于東西兩省，文武閒職，公府散佐，無事冗官，或數旬方應一直，或朔望止於暫朝。

translations.literal: In the eastern and western two provinces, civil and military idle posts, scattered assistants in public offices, and superfluous officials with nothing to do—some answered a single duty only after several tens of days, or on the first and fifteenth merely attended a brief court.
translations.idiomatic: In the two capitals' ministries, idle civil and military posts and redundant staff might answer one duty in weeks or attend court only on the first and fifteenth.

sentences.zh: 及其考日，更得四年為限。

translations.literal: When their examination day came, they again received a four-year limit.
translations.idiomatic: Their review again allowed four years.

sentences.zh: 是則一紀之中，便登三級。

translations.literal: Thus within one twelve-year cycle they could ascend three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In one twelve-year cycle they rose three ranks.

sentences.zh: 彼以實勞劇任，而遷貴之路至難；

translations.literal: Those, by real toil in heavy duty, found the road to noble advancement extremely hard;
translations.idiomatic: Men in hard real posts found promotion very hard;

sentences.zh: 此以散位虛名，而升陟之方甚易。

translations.literal: these, by scattered posts and empty titles, found the way of ascent very easy.
translations.idiomatic: idle title-holders found it very easy.

sentences.zh: 何內外之相縣，令厚薄之若此！

translations.literal: How wide the gap between inner and outer, making thick and thin like this!
translations.idiomatic: How vast the gap between inner and outer service!

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：「仁義忠信，天爵也；

translations.literal: Mencius said: "Benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and faith are Heaven's nobility;
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, "Benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and faith are Heaven's rank;

sentences.zh: 公卿大夫，人爵也。

translations.literal: dukes, ministers, and grandees are man's nobility.
translations.idiomatic: dukes, ministers, and grandees are man's rank.

sentences.zh: 古之人，修其天爵而人爵從之。

translations.literal: The men of old cultivated their Heaven's nobility and man's nobility followed.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients cultivated Heaven's rank and man's rank followed.

sentences.zh: 」故雖文質異時，汙隆殊世，莫不寶茲名器，不以假人。

translations.literal: " Therefore though culture and substance differed by age and rise and fall differed by era, none failed to treasure these name and vessels and not lend them to others.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in every age they treasured rank and title and did not lend them lightly.

sentences.zh: 是以賞罰之科，恆自持也。

translations.literal: Hence the statutes of reward and punishment were always strictly upheld.
translations.idiomatic: Reward and punishment were always strictly upheld.

sentences.zh: 乃至周之藹藹，五叔無官；

translations.literal: Even in the Zhou's flourishing age, the five uncles had no office;
translations.idiomatic: Even in flourishing Zhou the five uncles had no posts;

sentences.zh: 漢之察察，館陶徒請。

translations.literal: in the Han's scrutiny, Guantao merely requested.
translations.idiomatic: under Han scrutiny, Guantao only made a request.

sentences.zh: 誠以賞罰一差，則無以懲勸；

translations.literal: Truly, if reward and punishment were off by one degree, there would be no way to warn and encourage;
translations.idiomatic: If reward and punishment slipped, there was no warning or encouragement;

sentences.zh: 至公暫替，則覬覦相欺。

translations.literal: if supreme fairness were briefly set aside, covetous eyes would deceive one another.
translations.idiomatic: if fairness faltered, men schemed against one another.

sentences.zh: 故至慎至惜，殷勤若此。

translations.literal: Therefore they were most cautious and sparing, earnest to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Hence they were cautious and sparing to this degree.

sentences.zh: 況乎親非肺腑，才乖秀逸，或充單介之使，始無汗馬之勞；
