translations.literal: How much more when kin were not of one's flesh and blood, talent fell short of excellence, some filled a lone envoy's post yet from the start had no sweat-of-horse toil;
translations.idiomatic: Much less when kin were not close, talent was slight, some held a lone envoy's post without battle toil;

sentences.zh: 或說興利之規，終縣十一之潤。

translations.literal: or spoke plans for increasing profit, yet in the end hung up an elevenfold gain.
translations.idiomatic: or touted profit plans that ended as empty elevenfold gains.

sentences.zh: 皆虛張無功，妄指贏益；

translations.literal: All inflated merit without achievement and falsely pointed to surplus;
translations.idiomatic: All boasted false merit and false profit;

sentences.zh: 坐獲數階之官，籍成通顯之貴。

translations.literal: sitting they gained several ranks of office and on the rolls became passably eminent nobles.
translations.idiomatic: they gained several ranks by fraud and rose to visible rank.

sentences.zh: 於是巧詐萌生，偽辯鋒出，役萬慮以求榮，開百方而逐利。

translations.literal: Thereupon crafty fraud sprouted, false argument flashed forth, they expended ten thousand schemes to seek glory and opened a hundred paths to chase profit.
translations.idiomatic: Then fraud and sharp talk flourished; men spent endless schemes for glory and profit.

sentences.zh: 抑之則其流已往，引之則有何紀極！

translations.literal: Suppress it and the current had already passed; draw it out—what limit could there be!
translations.idiomatic: Check it and the flood had passed; indulge it—where would it end!

sentences.zh: 夫琴瑟在於必和，更張求其適調。

translations.literal: Zither and lute lie in necessary harmony; restring and seek the proper tuning.
translations.idiomatic: Like a zither, government needs retuning to harmony.

sentences.zh: 去者既不可追，來者猶或宜改。

translations.literal: What is gone cannot be pursued; what comes may still be fit to change.
translations.idiomatic: The past cannot be chased; the future may still be changed.

sentences.zh: 案《周官》：太宰之職，歲終，則令官府各正所司，受其會計，聽其事致而詔于王。

translations.literal: According to the Zhou Offices: the Grand Steward's duty—at year's end he ordered each office to rectify its charge, receive its accounts, hear its accomplishments reported, and announce them to the king.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Offices say: at year's end the Grand Steward had each office correct its charge, settle accounts, report results, and announce them to the king.

sentences.zh: 三歲，則大計群吏之政而誅賞之。

translations.literal: Every three years he made a great reckoning of the officials' governance and rewarded or punished them.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years he reckoned officials' governance and rewarded or punished them.

sentences.zh: 愚謂今可粗依其准。

translations.literal: I humbly think that today one might roughly follow that standard.
translations.idiomatic: I think we might roughly follow that standard today.

sentences.zh: 見居官者，每歲終，本曹皆明辨在官日月，具核才行能否，審其實用。

translations.literal: For those presently in office, at each year's end their home bureau should clearly distinguish months and days in post, fully verify ability and conduct, can or cannot, and examine real usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Each year every bureau should record months in post, judge ability and conduct, and note real usefulness.

sentences.zh: 而注其上下，遊辭宕說，一無取焉。

translations.literal: Then record their upper and lower grades; idle talk and grand speech—take none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Record grades up or down; take no idle boasting.

sentences.zh: 列上尚書，覆其合否。

translations.literal: Submit lists to the Masters of Writing and review whether they fit.
translations.idiomatic: Submit lists to the Masters of Writing for review.

sentences.zh: 如有紕繆，即正而罰之，不得方復推詰委下，容其進退。

translations.literal: If there were error, correct and punish at once; one must not again push inquiry down and allow advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: On error, punish at once; do not pass cases down and let men slip through.

sentences.zh: 既定其優劣，善惡交分，經奏之後，考功曹別書于黃紙、油帛。

translations.literal: Once superior and inferior were fixed and good and bad divided, after memorial passed, the Merit Review Bureau should separately write on yellow paper and oiled silk.
translations.idiomatic: After grades were fixed and memorialized, Merit Review should write separate records on yellow paper and oiled silk.

sentences.zh: 一通則本曹尚書與令僕印署，留于門下；

translations.literal: One copy the home bureau's director and chief secretaries would seal and leave at the Gate Department;
translations.idiomatic: One copy the bureau director and chief secretaries sealed and kept at the Gate Department;

sentences.zh: 一通則以侍中黃門印署，掌在尚書。

translations.literal: one copy the Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate would seal and keep in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: one copy the Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate sealed and kept in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 嚴加緘密，不得開視。

translations.literal: Seal it strictly; it must not be opened and viewed.
translations.idiomatic: Seal it strictly; no one may open it.

sentences.zh: 考績之日，然後對共裁量。

translations.literal: On the day of merit review, only then judge together face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Only on review day should they judge together.

sentences.zh: 其外內考格，裁非庸管，乞求博議，以為畫一。

translations.literal: As for inner and outer examination rules, that is not a matter for common handling; I beg broad discussion to make one standard.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer review rules need broad discussion for one standard.

sentences.zh: 若殊謀異策，事關廢興，遐邇所談，物無異議者，自可臨時斟酌，匪拘恆例。

translations.literal: If there were special plans and unusual policies touching rise or fall, discussed far and near with no dissent, one might of course weigh them at the time and not be bound by constant precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Unique policies on which all agreed might be weighed at the time, not by fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 至如援流引比之訴，貪榮求級之請。

translations.literal: As for appeals citing precedent streams, and requests greedy for glory and seeking rank.
translations.idiomatic: As for precedent-chasing appeals and greedy requests for rank.

sentences.zh: 如不限以關鍵，肆其傍通，則蔓草難除，涓流遂積，穢我彝章，撓茲大典，謂宜明加禁斷，以全至化。

translations.literal: If not limited by key and gate but allowed side passages at will, then creeping grass would be hard to remove, trickling streams would accumulate, defiling our great statutes and disturbing this great canon—I say they should be clearly forbidden to preserve perfect transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Without strict limits, abuses would spread and defile the law; they should be clearly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 詔付外博議，以為永式。

translations.literal: An edict sent it out for broad outer discussion to make an everlasting model.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent it out for broad discussion as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 竟無所改。

translations.literal: In the end nothing was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing was changed in the end.

sentences.zh: 時梁武弟子西豐侯正德來降，寶夤表曰：「正德既不親親，安能親人。

translations.literal: At the time Liang Wudi's younger brother, Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde, came over in surrender; Baoyin memorialized: "Zhengde, being unfilial to kin, how can he be kin to others?
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Wudi's brother Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde surrendered, Baoyin wrote, "Zhengde was unfilial to kin—how can he be loyal to others?

sentences.zh: 脫包此凶醜，置之列位，百官是象，其何誅焉？

translations.literal: If we release and wrap up this vicious villain and place him in the ranks, the hundred officials are the model—how can he be punished?
translations.idiomatic: If this villain is seated among officials, what example do we set for punishment?

sentences.zh: 臣釁結禍深，痛纏骨髓，日暮途遙，報復無日，豈區區於一豎哉！

translations.literal: Your servant's feud runs deep, pain coils the marrow, the road at dusk is far, and the day of revenge has no date—how could it be only about one petty fellow!
translations.idiomatic: My feud runs deep and revenge seems far—but this is not about one petty man alone!

sentences.zh: 但才雖庸近，職居獻替，愚衷寸抱，敢不申陳。

translations.literal: Yet though talent is mediocre and near, the post is remonstrance and replacement; this foolish heart's inch of feeling—I dare not fail to state it.
translations.idiomatic: Though my talent is slight, my post is remonstrance; I dare not stay silent.

sentences.zh: 」正德既至京師，朝廷待之尤薄，歲餘，還叛。

translations.literal: " When Zhengde reached the capital, the court treated him very coldly; after more than a year he rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde reached the capital, was treated coldly, and after a year rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 初，秦州城人薛伯珍、劉慶、杜遷等反，執刺史李彥，推莫折大提為首，自稱秦王。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qinzhou city men Xue Bozhen, Liu Qing, Du Qian, and others rebelled, seized Inspector Li Yan, and pushed Moqi Dati as leader, styling themselves King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou men Xue Bozhen, Liu Qing, and Du Qian rebelled, seized Inspector Li Yan, and made Moqi Dati King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 大提尋死，其第四子念生竊號天子，年曰天建。

translations.literal: Dati soon died; his fourth son Niansheng usurped the title Son of Heaven, era name Tianjian.
translations.idiomatic: Dati soon died; his fourth son Niansheng styled himself emperor, era Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 置官寮，以息阿胡為太子，其兄阿倪為西河王，弟天生為高陽王，伯珍為東郡王，安保為平陽王。

translations.literal: He set up officials; made Xi Ahu crown prince, his elder brother Ani King of Xihe, younger brother Tiansheng King of Gaoyang, Bozhen King of Dongjun, and Anbao King of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He set up offices: Xi Ahu crown prince, Ani King of Xihe, Tiansheng King of Gaoyang, Bozhen King of Dongjun, Anbao King of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 天生率眾出隴東，遂寇雍州，屯于黑水。

translations.literal: Tiansheng led troops out of Longdong and then raided Yong Province, encamping at Heishui.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng marched from Longdong, raided Yong, and camped at Heishui.

sentences.zh: 朝廷甚憂之，除寶夤開府、西道行台，為大都督，西征。

translations.literal: The court was deeply worried; Baoyin was made Commissioner with staff, Western Route Mobile Secretariat, Grand Commander, and sent west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Baoyin commissioner with staff, western route commander, and sent him west.

sentences.zh: 明帝幸明堂以餞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming visited the Bright Hall to give him farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming saw him off at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 寶夤與大都督崔延伯擊天生大破之，追奔至小隴。

translations.literal: Baoyin with Grand Commander Cui Yanbo struck Tiansheng and routed him badly, pursuing to Xiaolong.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin and Grand Commander Cui Yanbo routed Tiansheng and pursued to Xiaolong.

sentences.zh: 進討高平賊帥万俟醜奴于安定，更有負捷。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Gaoping bandit chief Wan Qichounu at Anding, he again had a victory to his credit.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Wan Qichounu at Anding and won again.

sentences.zh: 時有天水人呂伯度兄弟始共念生同逆，後與兄眾保于顯親聚眾討念生。

translations.literal: At the time Tianshui man Lu Baidu and his brothers had first joined Niansheng in rebellion, then with his elder brother Zhongbao at Xianqin gathered troops to attack Niansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Baidu of Tianshui first joined Niansheng, then with his brother Zhongbao at Xianqin raised troops against him.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，奔于胡琛。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle, he fled to Hu Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, he fled to Hu Chen.

sentences.zh: 琛以伯度為大都督、秦王，資其士馬，還征秦州。

translations.literal: Chen made Baidu Grand Commander and King of Qin, supplied him with troops and horses, and sent him back to campaign in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen made Baidu grand commander and King of Qin, gave him troops, and sent him back into Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 大破念生將杜粲于成紀，又破其金城王莫折普賢于水洛城，遂至顯親。

translations.literal: He routed Niansheng's general Du Can at Chengji and again routed his King of Jincheng Moqi Puxian at Shuilo City, then reaching Xianqin.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Du Can at Chengji and Moqi Puxian at Shuilo, then reached Xianqin.

sentences.zh: 念生率眾身自拒戰，又大敗。

translations.literal: Niansheng led troops in person to resist and was again badly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Niansheng fought in person and was routed again.

sentences.zh: 伯度乃背胡琛，遣其兄子忻和率騎東引大軍。

translations.literal: Baidu then turned against Hu Chen and sent his nephew Xinhe to lead cavalry east to draw the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Baidu turned on Hu Chen and sent his nephew Xinhe east to summon the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 念生事迫，乃詐降於寶夤。

translations.literal: Niansheng, pressed, then feigned surrender to Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed, Niansheng feigned surrender to Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉伯度立義之功，授涇州刺史、平秦郡公。

translations.literal: The court praised Baidu's merit in upholding righteousness and made him Inspector of Jing and Duke of Pingqin.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised Baidu's loyalty and made him Inspector of Jing and Duke of Pingqin.

sentences.zh: 而大都督元脩義、高聿停軍隴口，久不西進。

translations.literal: But Grand Commander Yuan Xiuyi and Gao Yu halted the army at Longkou and long did not advance west.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander Yuan Xiuyi and Gao Yu halted at Longkou and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 念生復反，伯度為醜奴所殺。

translations.literal: Niansheng rebelled again; Baidu was killed by Chounu.
translations.idiomatic: Niansheng rebelled again; Chounu killed Baidu.

sentences.zh: 故賊勢更甚，寶夤不能制。

translations.literal: Therefore the bandit power grew worse and Baoyin could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew stronger and Baoyin could not control them.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年，除寶夤侍中、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、假大將軍、尚書令，給前後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaochang, Baoyin was made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Equal to Three Departments, Acting Great General, Director of the Masters of Writing, and given front and rear processional music.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochang 2 made Baoyin palace attendant, general of agile cavalry, equal to three departments, acting great general, director of the masters of writing, with full processional music.

sentences.zh: 寶夤初自黑水，終至平涼，與賊相對，年年攻擊，賊亦憚之。

translations.literal: From Heishui at first to Pingliang at last, Baoyin faced the bandits year by year in attack; the bandits also feared him.
translations.idiomatic: From Heishui to Pingliang Baoyin fought the rebels yearly; they feared him too.

sentences.zh: 關中保全，寶夤之力。

translations.literal: That Guanzhong was preserved was Baoyin's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong was preserved by Baoyin's effort.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，除司空公。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he was made Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, first month, he was made Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 出師既久，兵將疲弊，是月大敗，還雍州。

translations.literal: The campaign had lasted long; troops and generals were worn; that month he was badly defeated and returned to Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: The army was worn; that month he was routed and returned to Yong.

sentences.zh: 有司處寶夤死罪，詔恕為編戶。

translations.literal: The authorities sentenced Baoyin to death; an edict pardoned him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The court sentenced him to death; an edict reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 四月，除征西將軍、雍州刺史、開府、西討大都督，自關以西，皆受節度。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was made General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yong, Commissioner with staff, Western Expedition Grand Commander; from west of the Pass all obeyed his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he became general who pacifies the west, inspector of Yong, commissioner, western expedition commander; all west of the Pass obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 九月，念生為其常山王杜粲所殺，合門皆盡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Niansheng was killed by his King of Changshan Du Can; his whole house was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Du Can killed Niansheng and wiped out his house.

sentences.zh: 粲降寶夤。

translations.literal: Can surrendered to Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Can surrendered to Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 十月，除尚書令，復其舊封。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was made Director of the Masters of Writing and his old fief was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was director of the masters of writing and his old fief was restored.

sentences.zh: 時山東、關西，寇賊充斥，王師屢北，人情沮喪。

translations.literal: At the time east of the mountains and west of the Pass were filled with bandits; the royal army was repeatedly beaten north; hearts were discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits filled Shandong and Guanxi; imperial armies kept losing; morale sank.

sentences.zh: 寶夤自以出師累年，糜費尤廣，一旦覆敗，慮見猜責，內不自安。

translations.literal: Baoyin himself thought that campaigning for years had wasted expense on a vast scale; once overturned in defeat, he feared blame and suspicion and was inwardly ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After years of costly war and one great defeat, he feared blame and grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 朝廷頗亦疑阻。

translations.literal: The court also was quite suspicious and obstructive.
translations.idiomatic: The court too grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 及遣御史中尉酈道元為關中大使，寶夤謂密欲取己，將有異圖，問河東柳楷。

translations.literal: When Imperial Censor-in-Chief Li Daoyuan was sent as envoy to Guanzhong, Baoyin thought he secretly meant to seize him and would have a different plot; he asked Hedong's Liu Kai.
translations.idiomatic: When Imperial Censor-in-Chief Li Daoyuan came as Guanzhong envoy, Baoyin feared arrest and asked Liu Kai of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 楷曰：「大王齊明帝子，天下所屬，今日之舉，實允人望。

translations.literal: Kai said: "Great King, son of Qi Emperor Ming, is whom the realm looks to; today's move truly fits men's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Kai said, "You are Qi Emperor Ming's son and the realm looks to you; this move fits men's hopes.

sentences.zh: 且謠言：'鸞生十子九子攵段，一子不攵段關中亂。

translations.literal: Moreover a rumor: 'Luan bore ten sons; nine sons were put to death, one son was not put to death—Guanzhong in turmoil.'
translations.idiomatic: A rumor says, 'Luan bore ten sons; nine were executed, one was not—Guanzhong fell into turmoil.'

sentences.zh: ' 武王有亂臣十人，亂者理也，大王當理關中，何所疑慮？」

translations.literal: ' King Wu had ten disorderly ministers; disorder means to govern—Great King should govern Guanzhong; what is there to doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: King Wu had ten 'disorderly' ministers—disorder means to govern; you should govern Guanzhong; why doubt?"

sentences.zh: 道元行達陰盤驛，寶夤密遣其將郭子恢等攻殺之，而詐收道元屍，表言白賊所害。

translations.literal: Daoyuan, traveling, reached Yinpan Post; Baoyin secretly sent his generals Guo Zihui and others to attack and kill him, then falsely collected Daoyuan's corpse and memorialized that white bandits had killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At Yinpan Post Baoyin secretly had Guo Zihui kill Daoyuan, then claimed white bandits had done it.

sentences.zh: 遂反，僭舉大號，大赦其部內，稱隆緒元年，立百官。

translations.literal: He then rebelled, usurped a great title, amnestied his territory, styled the era Longxu year one, and set up the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: He rebelled, declared an era, amnestied his territory, styled Longxu year one, and set up offices.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書僕射、行台長孫承業討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Mobile Secretariat Chief Changsun Chengye to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Vice Director and Mobile Secretariat Chief Changsun Chengye against him.

sentences.zh: 時北地毛鴻賓與其兄遐糾率鄉義，將討寶夤。

translations.literal: At the time Beidi's Mao Hongbin and his elder brother Xia led village righteousness to attack Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hongbin of Beidi and his brother Xia led local levies against Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 寶夤遣其將侯終德往攻遐。

translations.literal: Baoyin sent his general Hou Zhongde to attack Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin sent Hou Zhongde against Xia.

sentences.zh: 終德還圖寶夤，軍至白門，寶夤始覺。

translations.literal: Zhongde turned to plot against Baoyin; the army reached White Gate and Baoyin only then realized it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde turned on Baoyin; when his army reached White Gate Baoyin realized it.

sentences.zh: 與終德戰，敗，攜公主及其少子與部下百餘騎從後門出，遂奔万俟醜奴。

translations.literal: He fought Zhongde, was defeated, took the princess and his youngest son with a little more than a hundred riders out the rear gate, and fled to Wan Qichounu.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, he took the princess and youngest son with a hundred riders out the rear gate and fled to Wan Qichounu.

sentences.zh: 醜奴以寶夤為太傅。

translations.literal: Chounu made Baoyin Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu made Baoyin grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 爾硃天光遣賀拔嶽等破醜奴于安定，追禽醜奴及寶夤，並送京師。

translations.literal: Erzhu Tianguang sent Heba Yue and others to defeat Chounu at Anding, pursued and captured Chounu and Baoyin, and sent them both to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang sent Heba Yue to defeat Chounu at Anding, captured Chounu and Baoyin, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔置閶闔門外都街中，京師士女聚觀，凡經三日。

translations.literal: An edict placed them in the central avenue outside Changhe Gate; capital gentlemen and ladies gathered to watch—for three days in all.
translations.idiomatic: They were displayed in the avenue outside Changhe Gate while the capital watched for three days.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李神俊、黃門侍郎高道穆並與寶夤素舊，二人相與左右，言于莊帝，雲其逆跡事在前朝，冀將救免。

translations.literal: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Li Shenjun and Yellow Gate Vice Director Gao Daomu were both old friends of Baoyin; the two sided with him and spoke to Emperor Zhuang, saying his rebellious traces belonged to the former dynasty and they hoped to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun and Gao Daomu, Baoyin's old friends, told Emperor Zhuang his treason was under the former reign and hoped to save him.

sentences.zh: 會應詔王道習時自外至，莊帝問道習在外所聞。

translations.literal: It happened that Responding-Edict Wang Daoxi had just come from outside; Emperor Zhuang asked what Daoxi had heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: Responding-Edict Wang Daoxi arrived; the emperor asked what he had heard outside.

sentences.zh: 道習曰：「唯聞陛下欲不殺蕭寶夤。

translations.literal: Daoxi said: "I only heard that Your Majesty does not wish to kill Xiao Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxi said, "I only heard that Your Majesty will not kill Xiao Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 人云李尚書、高黃門與寶夤周款，並居得言之地，必能全之。

translations.literal: People say Director Li and Yellow Gate Gao are intimate with Baoyin and both stand where speech carries weight—they can surely preserve him.
translations.idiomatic: People say Director Li and Yellow Gate Gao are close to Baoyin and can save him.

sentences.zh: 」道習因曰：「若謂寶夤逆在前朝，便將恕之；

translations.literal: " Daoxi then said: "If one says Baoyin's rebellion was in the former dynasty and will therefore be pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: Daoxi added, "If treason under the former reign excuses him,

sentences.zh: 敗在長安，為醜奴太傅，並非陛下禦曆之日？

translations.literal: was not his defeat at Chang'an, as Chounu's Grand Tutor, also not under Your Majesty's own reign?
translations.idiomatic: was not his defeat at Chang'an as Chounu's grand tutor under Your Majesty's reign too?

sentences.zh: 賊臣不翦，法欲安施？

translations.literal: A rebel minister not cut down—how is law to be applied?
translations.idiomatic: If rebel ministers are spared, how is law applied?

sentences.zh: 」帝然其言，乃於太僕駝牛署賜死。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words and therefore at the Grand Stud Camel and Ox Office granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and had him granted death at the Grand Stud Camel and Ox Office.

sentences.zh: 將刑，神俊攜酒就之敘故舊，因對之下泣。

translations.literal: As execution neared, Shenjun carried wine to him to speak of old times and wept facing him.
translations.idiomatic: Before execution Shenjun brought wine, spoke of old times, and wept.

sentences.zh: 寶夤夷然自持，了不憂懼，唯稱推天委命，恨不終臣節。

translations.literal: Baoyin bore himself calmly, not worried or afraid at all, only saying he entrusted himself to Heaven's mandate and regretted not finishing his minister's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was calm and unafraid, saying he submitted to fate and regretted not dying a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 公主攜男女就寶夤訣別，慟哭極哀，寶夤亦色貌不改。

translations.literal: The princess brought the boys and girls to Baoyin for farewell; she wept in utmost grief, yet Baoyin's color and bearing did not change.
translations.idiomatic: The princess came to farewell with the children, weeping bitterly; Baoyin's face did not change.

sentences.zh: 寶夤三子皆公主所生，並凡劣。

translations.literal: Baoyin's three sons were all born of the princess and were all mediocre.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin's three sons by the princess were all mediocre.

sentences.zh: 長子烈，復尚明帝妹建德公主，拜駙馬都尉，坐寶夤反，伏法。

translations.literal: The eldest son Lie again married Emperor Ming's younger sister Princess of Jiande, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, and because of Baoyin's rebellion was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Lie married Princess of Jiande, became commandant of the horse guards, and was executed for Baoyin's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 次子權與小子凱射戲，凱矢激，中之，死。

translations.literal: The second son Quan and the youngest Kai were shooting in play; Kai's arrow glanced and hit him, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Quan and youngest Kai were shooting; Kai's arrow glanced and killed Quan.

sentences.zh: 凱妻，長孫承業女也，輕薄無禮，公主數加罪責。

translations.literal: Kai's wife was daughter of Changsun Chengye, frivolous and without propriety; the princess repeatedly added blame and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's wife, Changsun Chengye's daughter, was frivolous; the princess often punished her.

sentences.zh: 凱竊銜恨，妻復惑說之。

translations.literal: Kai secretly harbored resentment, and his wife again misled and urged him.
translations.idiomatic: Kai secretly resented her; his wife egged him on.

sentences.zh: 天平中，凱遣奴害公主。

translations.literal: In Tianping, Kai sent a slave to kill the princess.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping Kai sent a slave to kill the princess.

sentences.zh: 乃轘凱於東市。

translations.literal: He was then dismembered by cart at the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismembered by cart at the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 妻梟首，家遂滅。

translations.literal: His wife's head was exposed; the house was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was exposed; the house was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 寶夤兄子贊。

translations.literal: Baoyin's nephew Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin's nephew Zan.

sentences.zh: 贊字德文，本名綜。

translations.literal: Zan, styled Dewen, original name Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Zan, styled Dewen, was originally named Zong.

sentences.zh: 初，梁武滅齊，齊廢主東昏侯寶卷宮人吳氏始孕，匿不言；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liang Wudi destroyed Qi, the palace woman Wu of Qi deposed lord Eastern Hunter Prince Baojuan had first become pregnant and hid it without speaking;
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Wudi destroyed Qi, palace woman Wu of deposed Eastern Hunter Prince Baojuan hid her pregnancy;

sentences.zh: 及生贊，梁武以為己子，封豫章王。

translations.literal: when Zan was born, Liang Wudi took him as his own son and enfeoffed him Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: when Zan was born Wudi treated him as his son and made him Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 及長，學涉有才思。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he studied broadly and had talent and thought.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was learned and clever.

sentences.zh: 其母告之以實。

translations.literal: His mother told him the truth.
translations.idiomatic: His mother told him the truth.

sentences.zh: 贊晝則談謔，夜則銜悲涕泣。

translations.literal: By day Zan would jest; by night he would hold grief and weep.
translations.idiomatic: By day he jested; by night he wept in grief.

sentences.zh: 有濟陰苗文寵、安定梁話，贊曲加禮接，割血自誓，布以心腹。

translations.literal: There were Jiyin's Miao Wenchong and Anding's Liang Hua; Zan treated them with special courtesy, cut blood to swear, and opened his inmost heart to them.
translations.idiomatic: He honored Jiyin's Miao Wenchong and Anding's Liang Hua, cut blood to swear, and made them confidants.

sentences.zh: 寵、話感其情義，深相然諾。

translations.literal: Wenchong and Hua were moved by his feeling and pledged deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchong and Hua were moved and pledged themselves deeply.

sentences.zh: 會元法僧以彭城叛入梁，梁武命贊都督江北諸軍事，鎮彭城。

translations.literal: When Yuan Faseng rebelled at Pengcheng and entered Liang, Liang Wudi ordered Zan to command all military affairs north of the Yangzi and garrison Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng rebelled at Pengcheng and entered Liang, Wudi made Zan commander north of the Yangzi at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時明帝遣安豐王延明、臨淮王彧討之，贊與寵、話夜奔延明。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Ming sent Prince of Anfeng Yanming and Prince of Linhuai Yu to attack; Zan with Wenchong and Hua fled by night to Yanming.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Prince of Anfeng Yanming and Prince of Linhuai Yu; Zan fled by night with Wenchong and Hua to Yanming.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年秋，屆於洛陽。

translations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Xiaochang he arrived at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, Xiaochang 1, he reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 陛見後，就館舉哀，追服三載。

translations.literal: After audience he went to his lodging and performed mourning, observing mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: After audience he lodged and mourned three years.

sentences.zh: 寶夤時在關西，遣使觀察，問其形貌，斂眉悲感。

translations.literal: Baoyin was then in Guanxi and sent an envoy to observe, asking about his appearance; he knit his brows in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin in Guanxi sent men to observe him and grieved at his likeness.

sentences.zh: 朝廷賞賜豐渥，禮遇隆厚，授司空，封高平郡公、丹楊王。

translations.literal: The court rewarded him richly and treated him with lofty courtesy, making him Director of Works, enfeoffing him Duke of Gaoping and King of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court richly rewarded him, made him director of works, Duke of Gaoping, and King of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤反，贊怖，欲奔白鹿山，至河橋，為北中所執。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled, Zan was afraid and wished to flee to Bailu Mountain; at Heqiao he was seized by the northern guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled Zan fled toward Bailu Mountain and was seized at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 朝議明其不相干預，仍蒙慰免。

translations.literal: Court discussion made clear he had not been involved and he still received comfort and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The court found him uninvolved and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 建義初，轉司徒，遷太尉，尚帝姊壽陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was transferred to Minister of State, then promoted to Grand Commandant, married the emperor's elder sister Princess of Shouyang the Long, and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianyi he became minister of state, then grand commandant, married Princess of Shouyang the Long, and was commandant of the horse guards.

sentences.zh: 出為都督齊州刺史、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He went out as Commissioner of Qizhou, General of Agile Cavalry, and Commissioner with staff equal to three departments.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as commissioner of Qizhou, general of agile cavalry, and commissioner equal to three departments.

sentences.zh: 寶夤見禽，贊拜表請寶夤命。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was captured, Zan submitted a memorial begging Baoyin's life.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was captured Zan begged for his life.

sentences.zh: 爾硃兆入洛，為城人趙洛周所逐。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang he was driven off by city man Zhao Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang city man Zhao Luozhou drove him off.

sentences.zh: 公主被錄送京，爾硃世隆欲相陵逼。

translations.literal: The princess was seized and sent to the capital; Erzhu Shilong wished to violate her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was seized for the capital; Erzhu Shilong meant to violate her.

sentences.zh: 公主守操被害。

translations.literal: The princess kept her integrity and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: She kept her integrity and was killed.

sentences.zh: 贊既棄州，為沙門，潛詣長白山。

translations.literal: Zan, having abandoned his province, became a monk and secretly went to Changbai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zan abandoned his province, became a monk, and went secretly to Changbai Mountain.

sentences.zh: 未幾，至陽平，病卒。

translations.literal: Before long, reaching Yangping, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, at Yangping, he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 贊機辯，文義頗有可觀，而輕薄俶儻，猶有父風。

translations.literal: Zan was quick in debate; in letters and meaning he had quite what was worth seeing, yet he was frivolous and unrestrained—still his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was quick-witted and literate, but frivolous like his father.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，迎其喪，以王禮與公主合葬嵩山。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai his coffin was brought back and he was buried with the princess at Mount Song with princely rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Putai his coffin returned and he was buried with the princess at Mount Song with princely rites.

sentences.zh: 元象初，吳人盜其喪還江東，梁武猶以為子，祔葬蕭氏墓焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, Wu men stole his coffin back to Jiangdong; Liang Wudi still treated him as his son and buried him beside the Xiao clan tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxiang Wu men stole his coffin to the south; Wudi still buried him as his son in the Xiao tombs.

sentences.zh: 贊，江南有子，在魏無後。

translations.literal: Zan had a son in Jiangnan; in Wei he had no heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zan had a son in the south; in Wei he left no heir.

sentences.zh: 蕭正表，字公儀，梁武帝弟臨川王宏之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhengbiao, styled Gongyi, was son of Liang Wudi's younger brother Prince of Linchuan Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhengbiao, styled Gongyi, was son of Wudi's brother Prince of Linchuan Hong.

sentences.zh: 在梁封山陰縣侯，位北徐州刺史，鎮鐘離。

translations.literal: In Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Shanyin and was Northern Xuzhou Inspector, garrisoning Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang he was Marquis of Shanyin, northern Xuzhou inspector at Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 正表長七尺九寸，雖質貌豐美，而性理短暗。

translations.literal: Zhengbiao was seven feet nine inches tall; though his substance and looks were rich and fine, his nature and mind were short and dim.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet nine inches, handsome but dull of mind.

sentences.zh: 初，梁武未有子，以正表兄西豐侯正德為子。

translations.literal: Earlier Liang Wudi had no son and took Zhengbiao's elder brother Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde as son.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wudi had no son and adopted Zhengbiao's brother Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 及自有子，正德歸本，私懷忿憾，以正光三年，背梁奔魏。

translations.literal: When he had his own son, Zhengde returned to his origin and privately harbored resentment; in the third year of Zhengguang he turned his back on Liang and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi had his own son, Zhengde returned home resentful; in Zhengguang 3 he fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏朝以其人才庸劣，不禮焉。

translations.literal: The Wei court, because his talent was mediocre and inferior, did not treat him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Wei treated him coldly as mediocre talent.

sentences.zh: 尋逃歸梁，梁武不之罪，封為臨賀王。

translations.literal: Soon he fled back to Liang; Liang Wudi did not punish him and enfeoffed him Prince of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fled back; Wudi did not punish him and made him Prince of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 侯景將濟江，知正德有恨，密與交通，許推為主，正德以船迎之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was about to cross the Yangzi he knew Zhengde bore a grudge and secretly communicated with him, promising to push him as lord; Zhengde met him with boats.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing, knowing Zhengde's grudge, secretly promised him the throne; Zhengde met him with boats.

sentences.zh: 景度，攻揚州。

translations.literal: Jing crossed and attacked Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing crossed and attacked Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 正表聞正德為侯景所推，盤桓不赴援。

translations.literal: Zhengbiao heard Zhengde was pushed by Hou Jing and lingered without going to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengbiao heard Zhengde was Hou Jing's choice and did not march to rescue.

sentences.zh: 景尋以正表為南兗州刺史，封南郡王。

translations.literal: Jing soon made Zhengbiao Inspector of Southern Yanzhou and enfeoffed him King of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Jing soon made Zhengbiao southern Yanzhou inspector and King of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 正表遂于歐陽立柵，斷梁援軍。

translations.literal: Zhengbiao then at Ouyang set a palisade and cut off Liang relief armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengbiao set a palisade at Ouyang and blocked Liang relief.

sentences.zh: 南兗州刺史南康王蕭會理遣兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Southern Yanzhou Inspector Prince of Nankang Xiao Huili sent troops and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yanzhou Inspector Prince of Nankang Xiao Huili defeated him.

sentences.zh: 正表走還鐘離，以武定七年，據州內屬，封蘭陵郡王。

translations.literal: Zhengbiao fled back to Zhongli; in the seventh year of Wuding he held the province and submitted within, and was enfeoffed King of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Zhongli; in Wuding 7 he submitted and was made King of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中、太子太保、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Commissioner with staff equal to three departments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was palace attendant, grand tutor of the heir, and commissioner equal to three departments.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司空公，諡曰昭烈。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Duke of Works, posthumous name Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously duke of works, posthumous name Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 子廣壽。

translations.literal: Son Guangshou.
translations.idiomatic: Son Guangshou.

sentences.zh: 蕭祗，字敬式，梁武帝弟南平王偉之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhi, styled Jingshi, was son of Liang Wudi's younger brother Prince of Nanping Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhi, styled Jingshi, was son of Wudi's brother Prince of Nanping Wei.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，美容儀。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and keen, with fine bearing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was clever and handsome.

sentences.zh: 在梁封定襄縣侯，位東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang and was Eastern Yangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang he was Marquis of Dingxiang and eastern Yangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 于時江左承平，政寬人慢。

translations.literal: At the time the lower Yangzi was at peace and government was lenient while people were lax.
translations.idiomatic: The lower Yangzi was at peace; government was lax and people were slow.

sentences.zh: 祗獨蒞以嚴切，梁武悅之，遷北兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhi alone governed with severity; Liang Wudi was pleased and transferred him to Northern Yanzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi alone governed strictly; Wudi was pleased and moved him to northern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，侯景圍建業，祗聞台城失守，遂來奔，以武定七年至鄴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Jianye; Zhi heard the capital had fallen and came over in flight; in the seventh year of Wuding he reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing 2, when Jing besieged Jianye, Zhi fled; in Wuding 7 he reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄令魏收、邢邵與相接對。

translations.literal: Qi Wenzang ordered Wei Shou and Xing Shao to receive and face him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wenzang had Wei Shou and Xing Shao receive him.

sentences.zh: 歷位太子少傅，領平陽王師，封清河郡公。

translations.literal: He passed through posts to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, led tutor to Prince of Pingyang, and was enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He became junior tutor of the heir, tutor to Prince of Pingyang, and Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，授右光祿大夫，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao he was made Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and led Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianbao he was right grand master of splendid happiness and director of the national university.

sentences.zh: 時梁元帝平侯景，復與齊通好，文宣欲放祗等還南。

translations.literal: At the time Liang Yuan Di had pacified Hou Jing and again had good relations with Qi; Wensuan wished to release Zhi and others to return south.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Yuan Di pacified Hou Jing and renewed ties with Qi, Wensuan meant to send Zhi south.

sentences.zh: 俄而西魏克江陵，遂留鄴。

translations.literal: Soon Western Wei took Jiangling and he was kept at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Western Wei took Jiangling and he stayed at Ye.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈中書監、車騎大將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Yangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously director of the secretariat, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and Yangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 子放，字希逸，隨祗至鄴。

translations.literal: Son Fang, styled Xiyi, followed Zhi to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Son Fang, styled Xiyi, followed Zhi to Ye.

sentences.zh: 祗卒，放居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: When Zhi died, Fang dwelt in mourning and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi died Fang mourned and was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 所居廬室前，有二慈烏來集，各據一樹為巢，自午以前，馴庭飲啄；

translations.literal: Before the mourning hut he lived in, two kindly crows came and gathered, each occupying one tree as nest; before noon they were tame in the courtyard drinking and pecking;
translations.idiomatic: Before his mourning hut two tame crows nested, one per tree, feeding in the courtyard before noon;

sentences.zh: 午後更不下樹。

translations.literal: after noon they no longer came down from the trees.
translations.idiomatic: after noon they never left the trees.

sentences.zh: 每臨時舒翅悲鳴，全似哀泣。

translations.literal: Each time they spread wings in mournful cry, entirely like weeping in grief.
translations.idiomatic: They spread their wings and cried like mourners.

sentences.zh: 家人則之，未嘗有闕。

translations.literal: The family followed this and never failed in observance.
translations.idiomatic: The family followed this without fail.

sentences.zh: 時以為至孝之感。

translations.literal: At the time it was thought the utmost feeling of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Men took it as utmost filial feeling.

sentences.zh: 服闋，襲爵。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武平中，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: In Wuping he was retained at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping he served at the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 放性好文詠，頗善丹青，因此在宮中披覽書史及近世詩賦，監畫工作屏風等雜物。

translations.literal: Fang by nature loved literary chant and was quite skilled at cinnabar-green painting; therefore in the palace he browsed histories and recent poetry and prose and supervised painting of screens and other miscellaneous works.
translations.idiomatic: Fang loved poetry and painting; in the palace he read histories and verse and supervised screen painting.

sentences.zh: 見知，遂被眷待。

translations.literal: Known and seen, he then received favor and generous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Noticed, he won favor.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子中庶子、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to junior mentor of the heir and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 蕭退，梁武帝弟司空、鄱陽王恢之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Tui, son of Liang Wudi's younger brother the Minister of Works and Prince of Poyang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tui was son of Wudi's brother Minister of Works Prince of Poyang Hui.

sentences.zh: 退在梁封湘潭侯，位青州刺史。

translations.literal: Tui in Liang was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangtan and was Qingzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang he was Marquis of Xiangtan and Qingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 建業陷，與從兄祗俱入東魏。

translations.literal: When Jianye fell he with his cousin Zhi both entered Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianye fell he and his cousin Zhi entered Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 齊天保中，位金紫光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: In Qi Tianbao he was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao he was grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and died.

sentences.zh: 子慨，深沈有體表，好學，善草隸書，南士中稱為長者。

translations.literal: Son Kai, deep and steady in bearing, loved learning, skilled in draft and clerical script—among southern gentlemen he was called an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Son Kai, grave in bearing, learned, skilled in draft and clerical script, was called an elder among southerners.

sentences.zh: 曆著作佐郎，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: He passed through Associate Author and was retained at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He was associate author and retained at the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 卒于司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: He died as Staff Gentleman of the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: He died as staff gentleman of the minister of state.

sentences.zh: 蕭泰，字世怡，亦恢之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Tai, styled Shiyi, was also son of Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tai, styled Shiyi, was also Hui's son.

sentences.zh: 在梁封豐城侯，位譙州刺史。

translations.literal: In Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Fengcheng and held the post of Qiaozhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang he was Marquis of Fengcheng and Qiaozhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 侯景襲而陷之，因被執，尋逃至江陵。

translations.literal: Hou Jing attacked and took it; he was captured, then soon fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing seized him; he escaped to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝平侯景。

translations.literal: Liang Emperor Yuan pacified Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yuan Di pacified Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 以泰為兼太常卿、桂陽內史。

translations.literal: Tai was made concurrent Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Interior Minister of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was made concurrent grand master of splendid happiness and interior minister of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 未至郡，屬於謹平江陵，遂隨兄修佐郢州。

translations.literal: Before he reached the commandery, Yu Jin took Jiangling; he then followed his elder brother Xiu to assist at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took office, Yu Jin took Jiangling; he followed his brother Xiu to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及修卒，即以泰為刺史。

translations.literal: When Xiu died, Tai was at once made inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu died, Tai became inspector.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史王琳襲泰，泰以州輸琳。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou Inspector Wang Lin attacked Tai; Tai surrendered the province to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou inspector Wang Lin attacked; Tai surrendered the province.

sentences.zh: 時陳武帝執政，徵為侍中，不就。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Emperor Wu held power and summoned him as attendant-in-ordinary, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu summoned him as attendant-in-ordinary; he refused.

sentences.zh: 乃奔齊，為永州刺史。

translations.literal: He then fled to Qi and was Yongzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Qi as Yongzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，大將軍權景宣略地河南，泰遂歸西魏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, Grand General Quan Jingxuan seized territory in Henan; Tai then returned to Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding 4, Quan Jingxuan seized Henan; Tai returned to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 以名犯周文帝諱，稱字焉。

translations.literal: Because his name violated Zhou Emperor Wen's taboo, he was addressed by his style.
translations.idiomatic: His name tabooed Zhou Wen Di; he was called by his style.

sentences.zh: 拜開府儀同三司，封義興郡公，授蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commissioner with the Grand Insignia, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, enfeoffed Duke of Yixing commandery, and made Cai prefecture inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was commissioner equal to the three dukes, duke of Yixing, and Cai inspector.

sentences.zh: 政存簡惠，深為吏人所安。

translations.literal: His government preserved simplicity and kindness and deeply reassured officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was simple and kind; officials and people were at ease.

sentences.zh: 卒官，子寶嗣。

translations.literal: He died in office; son Bao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; son Bao inherited.

sentences.zh: 寶字季珍，美風儀，善談笑，未弱冠，名重一時。

translations.literal: Bao, styled Jizhen, had fine bearing and was skilled at witty talk; before the capping age his name weighed on the age.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, styled Jizhen, was handsome and witty; before capping age he was famed.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝輔政，引為丞相府典簽。

translations.literal: When Sui Emperor Wen aided the government, he was drawn as chief clerk of the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui Wen Di aided the government, he was chief clerk of the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，至吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he rose to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang he rose to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 後坐太子勇事誅，時人冤之。

translations.literal: Later he was executed for the affair of Crown Prince Yong; people of the time thought it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was executed in Crown Prince Yong's affair; the age thought it unjust.

sentences.zh: 蕭捴，字智遐，梁武帝弟安成王秀之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Hui, styled Zhiyao, was son of Liang Emperor Wu's younger brother Prince Ancheng Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hui, styled Zhiyao, was son of Liang Wu Di's brother Prince Ancheng Xiu.

sentences.zh: 性溫裕，有儀錶，在梁封永豐縣侯。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and generous, with dignified bearing; in Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongfeng county.
translations.idiomatic: Mild and generous, with dignified bearing; in Liang he was Marquis of Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣李諧、盧元明使梁。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent Li Xie and Lu Yuanming as envoys to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Li Xie and Lu Yuanming to Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝以捴辭令可觀，令兼中書侍郎，受幣於賓館。

translations.literal: Liang Emperor Wu, finding Hui's eloquence admirable, had him concurrently serve as vice director of the Secretariat and receive tribute at the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu Di admired his eloquence and had him receive envoys as vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曆黃門侍郎，累遷巴西、梓潼二郡守。

translations.literal: He passed through vice director of the Yellow Gate and rose in succession to prefect of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice director of the yellow gate and rose to Baxi and Zitong prefect.

sentences.zh: 及侯景作亂，武陵王紀稱尊號。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Prince Wuling Ji assumed the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Prince Wuling Ji took the throne.

sentences.zh: 時宗室在蜀，唯捴一人，封捴秦郡王。

translations.literal: Of the imperial clan in Shu at the time only Hui remained; Ji enfeoffed Hui Prince of Qin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hui of the clan remained in Shu; Ji made him Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 紀率眾東下，以捴為尚書令、征西大將軍、都督、益州刺史，守成都。

translations.literal: Ji led his host east; he made Hui Secretariat Director, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, area commander, and Yizhou inspector, to hold Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji marched east, made Hui secretariat director, grand general who pacifies the west, area commander, and Yizhou inspector at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 又令梁州刺史楊乾運守潼州。

translations.literal: He also ordered Liangzhou Inspector Yang Qianyun to hold Tong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Liangzhou inspector Yang Qianyun to hold Tong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 周文帝知蜀兵寡弱，遣大將軍尉遲迥總眾討之。

translations.literal: Zhou Emperor Wen knew Shu troops were few and weak and sent Grand General Yuchi Jiong to command the host against them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen Di sent grand general Yuchi Jiong against the weak Shu host.

sentences.zh: 迥入劍閣，長驅至成都。

translations.literal: Jiong entered Jian'ge and drove straight to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong entered Jian'ge and drove to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 捴見兵不滿萬人，而倉庫空竭，於是率文武於益州城北，共迥升壇歃血立盟，以城歸魏。

translations.literal: Hui saw troops under ten thousand and storehouses empty; he then led civil and military officials north of Yizhou city, together with Jiong ascended the altar, drank blood, and made alliance, surrendering the city to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: With under ten thousand troops and empty stores, he led officials north of the city, swore alliance with Jiong, and surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 授侍中、開府儀同三司，封歸善縣公。

translations.literal: He was appointed attendant-in-ordinary and commissioner equal to the three dukes, enfeoffed Duke of Guishan county.
translations.idiomatic: He was attendant-in-ordinary, commissioner equal to the three dukes, and duke of Guishan.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝踐阼，進爵黃台郡公。

translations.literal: When Zhou Emperor Min succeeded, his rank rose to Duke of Huangtai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Min Di succeeded, he became duke of Huangtai.

sentences.zh: 武成中，明帝令諸文儒於麟趾殿校定經史，仍撰《世譜》，捴亦豫焉。

translations.literal: In the Wucheng era, Emperor Ming ordered literary Confucians at Qilin Hall to collate the classics and histories and also compile the Genealogies of the Age; Hui also took part.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng, Ming Di had scholars collate classics at Qilin Hall and compile genealogies; Hui took part.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老，兼有疾疹，請在外著書，詔許之。

translations.literal: Soon, because his mother was old and he also had illness, he requested to write books outside court; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was old and he was ill; he asked to write outside court and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，授禮部中大夫，又以歸款功，別賜食多陵縣五百戶，收其租賦。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding he was made Grand Master of Rites in the Ministry of Rites; for merit in returning and submitting he was separately granted five hundred households of Duoling county to collect rents.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding 1 he was grand master of rites; for returning merit he received five hundred households' rent at Duoling.

sentences.zh: 三年，出為上州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as Shang prefecture inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was Shang prefecture inspector.

sentences.zh: 為政以禮讓為本，嘗至元日，獄中囚系，悉放歸家，聽三日然後赴獄。

translations.literal: His government took ritual yielding as its root; once on New Year's Day he released all prisoners in the jail to return home and allowed three days before they must return to prison.
translations.idiomatic: He governed by courtesy; on New Year's he sent all prisoners home for three days.

sentences.zh: 主者爭之，捴曰：「昔王長、虞延，見稱前史。

translations.literal: The chief officer disputed it; Hui said: "In former histories Wang Chang and Yu Yan were praised.
translations.idiomatic: The jailer objected; Hui said, "Wang Chang and Yu Yan were praised in history.

sentences.zh: 吾雖寡德，竊懷景行。

translations.literal: Though my virtue is slight, I secretly cherish their lofty conduct.
translations.idiomatic: My virtue is slight, but I cherish their example.

sentences.zh: 以之獲罪，彌所甘心。

translations.literal: To be punished for this I would be all the more willing.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment for this I would gladly accept.

sentences.zh: 」諸囚荷恩，並依限而至，吏人稱其惠化。

translations.literal: "The prisoners received his grace and all returned within the limit; officials and people praised his benevolent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners returned on time; officials and people praised his kindness.

sentences.zh: 秩滿向還，部人季漆等三百餘人上表，乞留更兩載。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he was about to return, more than three hundred people of the department, Ji Qi and others, submitted a memorial asking that he stay two more years.
translations.idiomatic: As his term ended, over three hundred led by Ji Qi asked him to stay two more years.

sentences.zh: 詔雖不許，甚嘉美之。

translations.literal: Though the edict did not permit it, the court greatly praised the beauty of it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict refused, but the court greatly praised it.

sentences.zh: 及捴入朝，屬置露門學。

translations.literal: When Hui entered court it happened that Lumen school was established.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui came to court, Lumen school was established.

sentences.zh: 武帝以捴與唐瑾、元偉、王褒等四人，俱為文學博士。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu made Hui, with Tang Jin, Yuan Wei, Wang Bao, and three others, all literary erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di made Hui, Tang Jin, Yuan Wei, Wang Bao, and three others literary erudites.

sentences.zh: 捴以母老，表請歸養私門，帝弗許。

translations.literal: Hui, because his mother was old, memorialized asking to return and nourish her in private; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to nurse his mother at home; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon he left office on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left office for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 曆少保、少傅，改封蔡陽郡公。

translations.literal: He passed through junior guardian and junior tutor and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Caiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was junior guardian and junior tutor and became duke of Caiyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，武帝舉哀于正武殿，贈使持節、大將軍、大都督、少傅、益州刺史，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: At his death Emperor Wu mourned at Zhengwu Hall and posthumously gave him bearer of the staff, grand general, area commander, junior tutor, and Yizhou inspector, with posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Wu Di mourned at Zhengwu Hall and gave him grand general, junior tutor, Yizhou inspector, posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 捴善草隸，書名亞王褒，算數醫方，咸亦留意。

translations.literal: Hui was skilled at cursive and clerical script; his calligraphic name was second to Wang Bao's; he also took note of arithmetic and medical recipes.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at cursive and clerical script, second to Wang Bao, and knew arithmetic and medicine.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦雜文數萬言，頗行於世。

translations.literal: Works of poetry, rhapsodies, and miscellaneous prose in tens of thousands of words circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of words of poetry and prose circulated.

sentences.zh: 子濟，字德成，少仁厚，頗好屬文。

translations.literal: Son Ji, styled Decheng, from youth was humane and generous and rather loved composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: Son Ji, styled Decheng, was humane and loved prose.

sentences.zh: 為東中郎將，從捴入朝。

translations.literal: He was Eastern Central Commander of Gentlemen and followed Hui to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was eastern central commander and followed Hui to court.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，除中外府記室，後至薄陽郡守。

translations.literal: When Zhou Emperor Xiao Min succeeded, he was made recorder of the inner and outer offices and later rose to prefect of Boyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Min Di succeeded, he was recorder of the inner and outer offices and later Boyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 蕭圓肅，字明恭，梁武帝之孫，武陵王紀之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Yuansu, styled Minggong, was grandson of Liang Emperor Wu and son of Prince Wuling Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yuansu, styled Minggong, was Liang Wu Di's grandson and Prince Wuling Ji's son.

sentences.zh: 風度淹雅，敏而好學。

translations.literal: His bearing was refined and elegant; he was quick and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Refined bearing; quick and studious.

sentences.zh: 紀稱尊號，封宜都王，除侍中。

translations.literal: When Ji assumed the imperial title, Yuansu was enfeoffed Prince of Yidu and made attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji took the throne, Yuansu was Prince of Yidu and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 紀下峽，令圓肅副蕭捴守成都。

translations.literal: When Ji went down the gorges he ordered Yuansu to assist Xiao Hui in holding Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji went down the gorges and left Yuansu to assist Hui at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥至，與捴俱降。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong arrived, he and Hui both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong arrived, he and Hui surrendered.

sentences.zh: 授開府儀同三司、侍中，封安化縣公。

translations.literal: He was appointed commissioner equal to the three dukes and attendant-in-ordinary, enfeoffed Duke of Anhua county.
translations.idiomatic: He was commissioner equal to the three dukes, attendant-in-ordinary, and duke of Anhua.

sentences.zh: 周明帝初，進棘城郡公，以歸款勳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Emperor Ming's reign he was advanced to Duke of Jicheng commandery for merit in returning and submitting.
translations.idiomatic: At Ming Di's accession he became duke of Jicheng for returning merit.

sentences.zh: 別賜食思君縣五百戶，收其租賦。

translations.literal: He was separately granted five hundred households of Sijun county to collect rents.
translations.idiomatic: He received five hundred households' rent at Sijun.

sentences.zh: 後拜咸陽郡守，甚有政績。

translations.literal: Later he was made Xianyang commandery prefect and had very fine administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Xianyang prefect with fine achievements.

sentences.zh: 尋改授太子少傅，作《少傅箴》。

translations.literal: Soon he was reassigned junior tutor of the crown prince and wrote the Admonition of the Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was crown prince junior tutor and wrote the Admonition of the Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 太子見而悅之，致書勞問。

translations.literal: The crown prince saw it and was pleased and sent a letter of thanks and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was pleased and sent thanks.

sentences.zh: 改授豐州刺史，尋進位上開府儀同大將軍，曆司宗中大夫、洛州刺史，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: He was reassigned Feng prefecture inspector, soon advanced to commissioner with the grand insignia equal in rank to the grand general, passed through grand master of the lineage in the Ministry of Rites and Luozhou inspector, and advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He was Feng inspector, then commissioner equal to the grand general, lineage grand master, Luozhou inspector, and grand general.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，授貝州刺史，以母老請歸就養，許之，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang he was made Beizhou inspector; because his mother was old he asked to return and nourish her and was permitted; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At Sui Kaihuang he was Beizhou inspector, asked to nurse his mother, was permitted, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷，又撰時人詩筆為《文海》四十卷、《廣堪》十卷、《淮海離亂志》四卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten scrolls; he also compiled contemporaries' poetry and brushwork into Literary Sea in forty scrolls, Broad Mirror in ten scrolls, and Records of Huaihai in Turmoil in four scrolls, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had collected works in ten scrolls and compiled Literary Sea, Broad Mirror, and Records of Huaihai in Turmoil, all circulating.

sentences.zh: 時大圜兄汝南王大封等猶未通謁。

translations.literal: At the time Dahuan's elder brother Prince of Runan Dafeng and others had still not presented court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Dahuan's brother Prince of Runan Dafeng had not yet presented audience.

sentences.zh: 元帝性忌刻，甚恨望之，乃使大圜召之。

translations.literal: Yuan Di's nature was jealous and harsh; he greatly resented them and therefore sent Dahuan to summon them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Di was jealous and resentful and sent Dahuan to summon them.

sentences.zh: 大圜即日曉諭，兩兄相繼出謁，元帝乃安之。

translations.literal: Dahuan that same day instructed them clearly; the two elder brothers in succession went out to audience and Yuan Di was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Dahuan instructed them; both brothers presented audience and Yuan Di was reassured.

sentences.zh: 大圜恐讒忻醖生，乃屏絕人事；

translations.literal: Dahuan feared slander might brew and therefore cut off human affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing slander, Dahuan cut off worldly affairs;

sentences.zh: 門客左右，不過三兩人。

translations.literal: retainers left and right were no more than two or three.
translations.idiomatic: he kept only two or three retainers.

sentences.zh: 不妄游狎，兄姊間，止箋疏而已。

translations.literal: He did not roam or play idly; between elder brothers and sisters he used only letters.
translations.idiomatic: He did not roam idly; with siblings he wrote only letters.

sentences.zh: 恆以讀《詩》、《禮》、《書》、《易》為事。

translations.literal: He constantly took reading the Odes, Rites, Documents, and Changes as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly read the Odes, Rites, Documents, and Changes.

sentences.zh: 元帝嘗自問《五經》要事數十條，大圜詞約指明，應答無滯。

translations.literal: Yuan Di once himself asked several dozen main points of the Five Classics; Dahuan's words were concise and pointed, his answers without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Di asked dozens of points on the Five Classics; Dahuan answered concisely without pause.

sentences.zh: 帝甚歎美之，因曰：「昔河間好學，爾既有之；

translations.literal: The emperor greatly sighed in admiration and said: "In former times Prince Hejian loved learning—you already have that;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him: "Prince Hejian loved learning—you have that;

sentences.zh: 臨淄好文，爾亦兼之。

translations.literal: Prince Linzi loved literature—you also combine that.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Linzi loved literature—you combine that too.

sentences.zh: 然有東平為善，彌高前載。

translations.literal: Yet in doing good like Prince Dongping you surpass the former records."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in doing good like Prince Dongping you surpass old examples."

sentences.zh: 」及於謹軍至，元帝乃令大封充使請和，大圜副焉，其實質也。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin's army arrived, Yuan Di ordered Dafeng to serve as envoy seeking peace and Dahuan as deputy—in truth they were hostages.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin arrived, Yuan Di sent Dafeng to sue for peace and Dahuan as deputy—in truth hostages.

sentences.zh: 出至軍所，信宿，元帝降。

translations.literal: They went out to the army camp; after two nights Yuan Di surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At the army camp, after two nights Yuan Di surrendered.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，大圜至長安，周文帝以客禮待之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wei Emperor Gong, Dahuan reached Chang'an; Zhou Emperor Wen received him with guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gong Di 2, Dahuan reached Chang'an; Zhou Wen Di received him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，大封為晉陵縣公，大圜始寧縣公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, Dafeng was Duke of Jinling county and Dahuan Duke of Shining county.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding 2, Dafeng was duke of Jinling and Dahuan duke of Shining.

sentences.zh: 尋加大圜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon Dahuan was further made Grand General of Cavalry and Chariots and commissioner equal to the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dahuan was grand general of cavalry and chariots, commissioner equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 俄而開麟趾殿，招集學士，大圜預焉。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Qilin Hall was opened and scholars gathered; Dahuan took part.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin Hall opened and gathered scholars; Dahuan took part.

sentences.zh: 《梁武帝集》四十卷、《簡文集》九十卷各止一本，江陵平後，並藏秘閣。

translations.literal: Collected Works of Liang Emperor Wu in forty scrolls and Brief Collected Works in ninety scrolls each existed in only one copy; after Jiangling was pacified they were both stored in the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu Di's collected works and brief collected works existed in single copies stored in the secret archive after Jiangling fell.

sentences.zh: 大圜入麟趾，方得見之，乃手寫二集，一年並畢，識者稱歎之。

translations.literal: When Dahuan entered Qilin he first saw them and thereupon copied both collections by hand, finishing both in one year; those who knew praised and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Qilin he copied both collections by hand in one year; observers marveled.

sentences.zh: 大圜深信因果，心安閒放，嘗云：

translations.literal: Dahuan deeply believed in karma; his mind was at ease and leisurely, and he once said:
translations.idiomatic: Deeply believing in karma, at ease and leisurely, he once said:

sentences.zh: 拂衣褰裳，無吞舟之漏網；

translations.literal: To shake out one's robes and lift one's skirt—no net of the state that swallows boats;
translations.idiomatic: Shake out robes and lift skirts—no state net that swallows boats;

sentences.zh: 掛冠縣節，慮我志之未從。

translations.literal: to hang up one's cap and suspend one's tally—lest my will has not yet followed.
translations.idiomatic: hang cap and tally—lest my will not yet be followed.

sentences.zh: 儻獲展禽之免，有美慈明之進。

translations.literal: If I might obtain Zhan Yi's release, there would be the fine advance of Ciming.
translations.idiomatic: If I might gain Zhan Yi's release, there would be Ciming's fine advance.

sentences.zh: 如蒙北叟之放，實勝濟南之征。

translations.literal: If I were favored with the northern old man's release, it would truly surpass the expedition against Ji'nan.
translations.idiomatic: The northern old man's release would truly surpass Ji'nan's expedition.

sentences.zh: 其故何哉？

translations.literal: What is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: What is the reason?

sentences.zh: 夫閭閻者有優遊之美，朝廷者有簪佩之累，蓋由來久矣。

translations.literal: In lanes and hamlets there is the beauty of ease; at court there is the burden of sash and cap—this has been so from of old.
translations.idiomatic: Hamlets have ease; courts have sash and cap—so from of old.

sentences.zh: 留侯追蹤于松子，陶硃成術于辛文，良有以焉。

translations.literal: Marquis Liu followed in the tracks of Master Pine; Tao Zhu mastered the art in Xin Wen—truly there was cause.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Liu followed Master Pine; Tao Zhu mastered Xin Wen—there was cause.

sentences.zh: 況乎智不逸群，行不高物，而欲辛苦一生，何其僻也。

translations.literal: How much more when wisdom does not surpass the crowd and conduct does not tower over things, yet one wishes to toil bitterly all one's life—how eccentric!
translations.idiomatic: When wisdom and conduct are ordinary, to toil all one's life—how eccentric!

sentences.zh: 豈如知足知止，蕭然無累。

translations.literal: How much better to know sufficiency and stop, carefree and without burden.
translations.idiomatic: Better to know sufficiency, carefree and unburdened.

sentences.zh: 北山之北，棄絕人間；

translations.literal: North of the northern mountain, abandoning the human world;
translations.idiomatic: North of the northern mountain, abandon the world;

sentences.zh: 南山之南，超逾世網。

translations.literal: south of the southern mountain, crossing beyond the world's net.
translations.idiomatic: south of the southern mountain, cross beyond the world's net.

sentences.zh: 面修原而帶流水，倚郊甸而枕平皋。

translations.literal: Facing the long plain and girded by flowing water, leaning on the suburban fields and resting on the level height.
translations.idiomatic: Face the long plain girded by water, lean on suburbs and rest on the level height.

sentences.zh: 築蝸舍于叢林，構環堵于幽薄。

translations.literal: Build a snail's hut in the thickets; erect a ring of walls in the secluded thicket.
translations.idiomatic: Build a snail hut in thickets; ring walls in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 近瞻煙霧，遠睇風雲。

translations.literal: Gaze near at mist and smoke; look far at wind and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Gaze at mist nearby; clouds afar.

sentences.zh: 藉纖草以廕長松，結幽蘭而援芳桂。

translations.literal: Borrow fine grass to shade tall pines; tie orchids and draw on fragrant cassia.
translations.idiomatic: Fine grass shades pines; orchids draw on cassia.

sentences.zh: 仰翔禽於百仞，俛泳鱗於千尋。

translations.literal: Look up at soaring birds a hundred fathoms high; look down at swimming fish a thousand fathoms deep.
translations.idiomatic: Birds soar a hundred fathoms up; fish swim a thousand down.

sentences.zh: 果園在後，開窗以臨花卉；

translations.literal: An orchard lies behind; open the window to overlook flowers;
translations.idiomatic: Orchard behind; open windows on flowers;

sentences.zh: 蔬圃居前，坐簷而看灌畎。

translations.literal: a vegetable garden lies before; sit under the eaves and watch irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: garden before; sit under eaves and watch irrigation.

sentences.zh: 二頃以供饘粥，十畝以給絲麻。

translations.literal: Two qing supply gruel; ten mu supply silk and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Two qing for gruel; ten mu for silk and hemp.

sentences.zh: 侍兒五三，可充糸任織；

translations.literal: Three or five serving maids can fill spinning and weaving;
translations.idiomatic: Three or five maids can spin and weave;

sentences.zh: 家僮數四，足代耕耘。

translations.literal: four or several household slaves suffice to replace plowing and hoeing.
translations.idiomatic: several slaves suffice for plowing.

sentences.zh: 沽酷牧羊，協潘生之志；

translations.literal: Buy wine and herd sheep—harmonizing with Master Pan's will;
translations.idiomatic: Buy wine and herd sheep like Master Pan;

sentences.zh: 畜雞種黍，應莊叟之言。

translations.literal: raise chickens and plant millet—answering Old Man Zhuang's words.
translations.idiomatic: raise chickens and millet like Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 獲菽尋汜氏之書，露葵征尹君之錄。

translations.literal: Gathering beans recalls the book of the Si clan; dewy greens cite Lord Yin's record.
translations.idiomatic: Beans recall the Si clan's book; greens cite Lord Yin's record.

sentences.zh: 烹羔豚而介春酒，迎伏臘而候歲時。

translations.literal: Cooking lamb and suckling pig with spring wine, welcoming the hidden and wax festivals and awaiting the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Lamb, suckling pig, and spring wine welcome the seasons.

sentences.zh: 披良書，采至賾，歌纂纂，唱烏烏。

translations.literal: Spread good books, gather the deepest essences, sing "Luxuriant," chant "Cawing."
translations.idiomatic: Read good books, gather deep essences, sing "Luxuriant" and "Cawing."

sentences.zh: 可以娛神，可以散慮。

translations.literal: This can delight the spirit and scatter cares.
translations.idiomatic: This delights the spirit and scatters cares.

sentences.zh: 有朋自遠，揚榷古今；

translations.literal: When friends come from afar, they weigh past and present;
translations.idiomatic: Friends from afar weigh past and present;

sentences.zh: 田畯相過，劇談稼穡。

translations.literal: when field officers visit, they talk keenly of crops.
translations.idiomatic: field officers talk keenly of crops.

sentences.zh: 斯亦足矣，樂不可支，永保性命，何畏憂責。

translations.literal: This too is enough; joy cannot be borne; forever preserve life and fate—why fear blame and responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: That is enough; joy is boundless; preserve life—why fear blame?

sentences.zh: 豈若蹙足入絆，申頸就羈。

translations.literal: How much less to cramp the feet entering fetters and stretch the neck to bonds.
translations.idiomatic: Why cramp the feet in fetters and stretch the neck to bonds?

sentences.zh: 遊帝王之門，趨宰衡之勢。

translations.literal: Roaming the doors of emperors and kings, hurrying to the power of chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Why roam emperors' doors and hurry to chief ministers' power?

sentences.zh: 不知飄塵之少選，寧覺年祀之斯須。

translations.literal: Not knowing that drifting dust passes in a moment—how can one feel that years pass in a trice?
translations.idiomatic: Drifting dust passes in a moment; years in a trice.

sentences.zh: 萬物營營，靡存其意；

translations.literal: The ten thousand things bustle busily, storing none of their intent;
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand things bustle, storing no intent;

sentences.zh: 天道昧昧，安可問哉？

translations.literal: the Way of Heaven is dim—how can it be questioned?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way is dim—how question it?

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 人生若浮，朝露寧俟。

translations.literal: Human life is like floating; morning dew—how can one wait?
translations.idiomatic: Life floats; morning dew—how wait?

sentences.zh: 長繩系景，實所願言。

translations.literal: To tie the sun with a long rope—that is truly the wish one speaks.
translations.idiomatic: Tie the sun with a long rope—that is the spoken wish.

sentences.zh: 執燭夜遊，驚其迅邁。

translations.literal: Holding candles for night roaming—one is startled at its swift advance.
translations.idiomatic: Night candles startle at swift advance.

sentences.zh: 百年幾何，擎跽曲拳。

translations.literal: A hundred years—how much? Kneeling with bent fists.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred years—how much? Bent knees and fists.

sentences.zh: 四時如流，俯眉躡足。

translations.literal: The four seasons like flowing water—bowed brows and tiptoe steps.
translations.idiomatic: Four seasons flow—bowed brows and tiptoe steps.

sentences.zh: 出處無成，語默奚當。

translations.literal: Going forth and withdrawing without achievement—speech and silence, how should one act?
translations.idiomatic: Going forth and withdrawing without achievement—how act in speech or silence?

sentences.zh: 非直丘明所恥，抑亦宣尼恥之。

translations.literal: Not only what Qiu Ming shamed, but also what Confucius shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Not only Qiu Ming's shame, but Confucius's too.

sentences.zh: 建德四年，除滕王逌友。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiande he was made friend to Prince Teng You.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande 4 he was friend to Prince Teng You.

sentences.zh: 逌嘗問大圜曰：「吾聞湘東王作《梁史》，有之乎？

translations.literal: You once asked Dahuan: "I hear Prince Xiangdong wrote a History of Liang—is there such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: You asked Dahuan, "Did Prince Xiangdong write a History of Liang?

sentences.zh: 餘傳乃可抑揚，帝紀奚若？

translations.literal: Others' biographies may be raised or lowered, but the imperial annals—how are they?
translations.idiomatic: Others' lives may be judged, but the imperial annals—how?

sentences.zh: 隱則非實，記則攘羊。

translations.literal: To conceal is not truth; to record is to seize the sheep."
translations.idiomatic: To conceal is untrue; to record is to seize the sheep."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「言之妄也。

translations.literal: He replied: "That is wild talk.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "That is wild talk.

sentences.zh: 如使有之，亦不足怪。

translations.literal: If there were such a thing, it would not be strange.
translations.idiomatic: If so, it would not be strange.

sentences.zh: 昔漢明為《世祖紀》，章帝為《顯宗紀》，殷鑒不遠，足為成例。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Ming wrote the Annals of the Founder; Zhang Di wrote the Annals of the Manifest Ancestor—a bronze mirror not far off, enough to be a completed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ming and Zhang Di wrote ancestor annals—a near mirror and precedent.

sentences.zh: 且君子之過，如日月之蝕，彰于四海，安得而隱之？

translations.literal: Moreover the gentleman's fault is like an eclipse of sun or moon, manifest to the four seas—how can it be concealed?
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman's fault is like sun or moon eclipsed to the four seas—how conceal?

sentences.zh: 如有不彰，亦安得不隱？

translations.literal: If something is not manifest, how can it not be concealed?
translations.idiomatic: If not manifest, how not conceal?

sentences.zh: 蓋子為父隱，直在其中，諱國之惡，抑又禮也。

translations.literal: In general the son conceals for the father; uprightness lies within; to veil the state's shame is also ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The son conceals for the father—uprightness within; veiling the state's shame is ritual."

sentences.zh: 」逌乃大笑。

translations.literal: You then laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: You laughed greatly.

sentences.zh: 後大軍拔晉州，或問大圜：「師遂克不？

translations.literal: Later when the great army took Jinyang, someone asked Dahuan: "Will the army surely conquer?
translations.idiomatic: When the army took Jinyang, someone asked Dahuan, "Will it conquer?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「高歡昔以晉州肇基偽跡，今本既拔矣，能無亡乎？

translations.literal: He replied: "Gao Huan once with Jinyang founded his false traces; now the root is already pulled—can there be no perishing?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Gao Huan founded his false rule from Jinyang; the root is pulled—how not perish?

sentences.zh: 所謂君以此始，必以此終。
