translations.literal: What is called 'the lord begins thus, he must end thus.'"
translations.idiomatic: As they say, 'begin thus, end thus.'"

sentences.zh: 」居數月，齊氏果滅。

translations.literal: After several months the Qi house indeed perished.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Qi perished.

sentences.zh: 聞者以為知言。

translations.literal: Those who heard deemed him one who knew how to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Hearers called him prescient.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，拜內史侍郎，卒于西河郡守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang he was made vice director of the Secretariat and died as Xihe commandery prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At Sui Kaihuang he was vice director of the secretariat and died as Xihe prefect.

sentences.zh: 撰《梁舊事》三十卷、《寓記》三卷、《士喪儀注》五卷、《要決》兩卷，並文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Old Affairs of Liang in thirty scrolls, Lodgings in three scrolls, Rites of Scholar Mourning in five scrolls, Essentials in two scrolls, and collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Old Affairs of Liang, Lodgings, Rites of Scholar Mourning, Essentials, and collected works.

sentences.zh: 大封位開府儀同三司、陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Dafeng held the rank of commissioner equal to the three dukes and was Chen prefecture inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Dafeng was commissioner equal to the three dukes and Chen inspector.

sentences.zh: 論曰：諸司馬以亂亡歸命，楚之最可稱乎！

translations.literal: Discussion: Of the various Sima who in chaos and ruin submitted and turned their allegiance, was Chuzhi the most praiseworthy?
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Of the Sima who fled chaos and submitted, was Chuzhi most praiseworthy?

sentences.zh: 其餘碌碌，未足論也。

translations.literal: The rest were mediocre and not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were mediocre—not worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 而以往代遺緒，並當位遇，可謂幸矣。

translations.literal: Yet to receive the surviving traces of former dynasties and all obtain suitable rank and favor—one may say they were fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet former-dynasty remnants all won rank—fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 劉昶猜疑懼禍，蕭夤亡破之餘，並潛骸竄影，委命上國。

translations.literal: Liu Chang, suspicious and fearing disaster, and Xiao Baoyin after ruin and defeat, both hid their bones and stole away their shadows, entrusting fate to the northern state.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, fearful, and Xiao Baoyin, ruined, hid and fled north.

sentences.zh: 俱稱曉了，盛當位遇。

translations.literal: All were called clever and greatly met rank and favor at court.
translations.idiomatic: All were called clever and greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 雖有枕戈之志，終無鞭墓之成。

translations.literal: Though they had the will to sleep with a spear at the pillow, in the end none achieved whipping the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Though they meant to sleep spear at pillow, none whipped the tomb.

sentences.zh: 昶諸子狂疏，喪其家業；

translations.literal: Chang's sons were wild and coarse and lost the family estate;
translations.idiomatic: Chang's sons were wild and lost the estate;

sentences.zh: 寶夤背恩忘義，梟鏡其心。

translations.literal: Bao and Baoyin betrayed kindness and forgot righteousness—their hearts were owl and mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and Baoyin betrayed kindness—owl-and-mirror hearts.

sentences.zh: 蕭贊臨邊脫身，晚去仇賊，寵祿頓臻，顛狽旋至，信吉凶之相倚也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zan at the frontier slipped away his body; late in leaving the foe-enemy, favor and salary came at once and collapse followed at once—truly fortune and misfortune lean on each other.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zan slipped the frontier, left foes late; favor came at once, collapse at once—fortune and misfortune lean together.

sentences.zh: 梁氏雲季，子弟奔亡。

translations.literal: The Xiao house at cloud's end; sons and younger kin fled in exile.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiao house at twilight; kin fled in exile.

sentences.zh: 王表動不由仁，胡顏之甚。

translations.literal: Wang Biao's impulses were not moved by benevolence—how shameless his face!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao acted without benevolence—how shameless!

sentences.zh: 祗、退、泰、捴、圓肅、大圜等雖羈旅異國，而終享榮名，非素有鎡基，懷文抱質，亦何能至於此也。

translations.literal: Zhi, Tui, Tai, Hui, Yuansu, Dahuan, and others though guests in another state yet finally enjoyed glorious names—not without having plow-furrow foundation, cherishing culture and embracing substance; how else could they reach this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, Tui, Tai, Hui, Yuansu, and Dahuan, guests abroad, yet won glory—not without culture and substance.

sentences.zh: 方武陵擁眾東下，任捴以蕭何之事。

translations.literal: When Prince Wuling mustered his host east, he entrusted Hui with Xiao He's affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wuling marched east, he entrusted Hui with Xiao He's role.

sentences.zh: 君臣之道既篤，家國之情亦隆。

translations.literal: The way of lord and minister was already deep; the feeling of family and state was also lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Lord and minister were deep; family and state feeling lofty.

sentences.zh: 金石不足比其心，河水不足明其誓。

translations.literal: Metal and stone could not compare to his heart; river waters could not clarify his oath.
translations.idiomatic: Metal and stone could not match his heart; rivers could not clarify his oath.

sentences.zh: 及魏安之至城下，旬日而智力俱竭，委金湯而不守，舉庸蜀而來王。

translations.literal: When Wei An arrived below the walls, within ten days wit and strength were both exhausted; he surrendered gold ramparts without defense and raised common Shu to come and be king.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei An reached the walls, wit and strength failed in ten days; he surrendered Chengdu and came to Wei as king.

sentences.zh: 若乃見機而作，誠有之矣；

translations.literal: If one speaks of seeing the moment and acting—indeed there was that;
translations.idiomatic: To see the moment and act—indeed there was that;

sentences.zh: 守節沒齒，則未可焉。

translations.literal: to keep integrity to the grave—that cannot be said.
translations.idiomatic: to keep integrity to the grave—that cannot be claimed.
